problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: polishes
polishing
had polished
polished
problem.explanation: 정답 D(polished): 인용문은 과거 습관을 회상하는 단순과거(swept, sorted)로 된 병렬 구조이므로, 세 번째 항목도 단순과거 polished가 되어야 시제와 형태가 모두 맞는다. A(polishes): 인터뷰 당시 시점에 맞춘 듯한 현재시제로, 과거 회상인 인용문의 시제와 맞지 않는다. B(polishing): 동명사·분사형으로, 병렬된 세 동사 중 이것만 형태가 달라 swept, sorted와 병렬이 깨진다. C(had polished): 'before he arrived'라는 종속절만 보면 그보다 먼저 일어난 일이라 과거완료가 맞아 보이지만, 같은 주어 I를 공유하는 단순과거 동사들과 함께 나열된 항목이라 문장 전체의 시제와 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: Choice D (polished) is correct. Inside the quotation, Varga describes her past daily routine with a series of verbs in the simple past: "swept" and "sorted." The third verb in that series has to be in the simple past too, so "polished" keeps both the tense and the parallel structure. Choice A (polishes) uses the present tense, which might seem to fit the time of the interview. But it clashes with the past-tense quotation. Choice B (polishing) is a gerund/participle, so it's the only item in the series with a different form, and the parallelism breaks. Choice C (had polished) seems logical if you focus only on the clause "before he arrived," since the polishing happened earlier. However, the word sits in a series with the simple-past verbs "swept" and "sorted," which share the subject "I." Switching to the past perfect would break the consistency of the whole sentence.

which: 병렬구조 전체 추적 후 국소적 과거완료 유혹(before he arrived) 배제
hardJudge.note: 인용문 내 swept, sorted, ___ 병렬이 명확하고 정답 D polished가 유일하게 시제·형태 모두 일치. A는 현재시제(인용 시제 불일치), B는 분사형(병렬 파괴), C had polished는 'before he arrived'만 보면 그럴듯하나 동일 주어의 단순과거 나열과 어긋나는 국소적 함정으로 레시피 요건 충족. 해설의 각 오답 근거도 정확. 가상 인물·상황으로 저작권 문제 없음. 다만 hard 수준으로는 비교적 수월한 편이며, 난이도는 주로 오답 C의 함정에서 발생함.

advisory.note: swept, sorted, polished로 단순과거 병렬이 이루어진다. C는 before절 때문에 그럴듯한 함정이 된다. 다만 병렬 단서가 바로 앞에 있어 hard로서는 다소 약하다.

problem.passage:
In the 1950s, glassblowers on the Venetian island of Murano guarded their furnace recipes closely, but one workshop's ledgers, rediscovered in a family attic in 2019, reveal how its master handled a shortage of imported soda ash. Having tested more than a dozen local plant ashes in small crucibles over a single winter, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the 1950s, glassblowers on the Venetian island of Murano guarded their furnace recipes closely, but one workshop's ledgers, rediscovered in a family attic in 2019, reveal how its master handled a shortage of imported soda ash. Having tested more than a dozen local plant ashes in small crucibles over a single winter, ______
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the crucibles showed the master glassblower Bruno Seguso that ash from saltwort produced the clearest melt.
the workshop's ledgers record that the master glassblower Bruno Seguso found ash from saltwort produced the clearest melt.
the master glassblower Bruno Seguso concluded that ash from saltwort produced the clearest melt.
Seguso's apprentice was told by the master glassblower that ash from saltwort produced the clearest melt.
problem.explanation: 분사구문 "Having tested ... in small crucibles over a single winter"의 의미상 주어는 실험을 한 사람, 즉 장인 Bruno Seguso이다. 따라서 주절 주어는 그가 되어야 한다. C가 정답이다. A: 수식어구 바로 앞의 무생물 명사 crucibles를 주어로 삼아, 도가니가 재를 시험한 것처럼 읽힌다. B: 지문 앞부분의 배경 명사 ledgers를 주어로 삼아, 장부가 시험한 것이 된다. Seguso는 that절 속에 묻혀 있어 의미상 주어가 될 수 없다. D: 사람이라 그럴듯해 보이지만 실험을 한 사람은 장인이지 견습생이 아니다. 이 문장대로라면 견습생이 시험한 것이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The opening phrase, "Having tested more than a dozen local plant ashes in small crucibles over a single winter," needs a subject that names whoever did the testing. Based on the passage, that is the master glassblower, Bruno Seguso. Choice C puts him right after the comma, so it is correct. Choice A makes "the crucibles" the subject. The crucibles held the ash; they didn't do the testing. Choice B makes "the workshop's ledgers" the subject. That wrongly says the ledgers ran the tests, and it buries Seguso inside a clause. Choice D makes the apprentice the subject. The apprentice is a person, so this one seems plausible, but the master is the one who did the testing, not the apprentice.

hardJudge.note: 분사구문 "Having tested ... in small crucibles over a single winter"의 행위자는 앞 문장의 "its master"로 지문 전체에서 추적해야 하며, C만 장인을 주어로 두어 정답이 옳다. A는 인접 무생물 명사 crucibles, B는 배경 명사 ledgers(Seguso는 that절 내부에 묻힘), D는 사람이지만 실험 주체가 아닌 apprentice를 주어로 두어 각각 현수수식어가 된다. 시제·구두점도 문제없고 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 설명한다. 소다회 부족 시 식물재(saltwort/barilla) 사용은 역사적으로 타당하며, 2019년 장부 발견·Bruno Seguso는 허구적 설정으로 사실 오류로 보기 어렵다. 형식은 SAT 표준에 부합하고 저작권 의심 없음. 단순 인접 일치가 아닌 의미상 행위자 판별(특히 D의 인간 오답)을 요구하므로 hard 적합.

advisory.note: C는 실험 행위자인 장인을 주절 주어로 삼으므로 정답입니다. D는 사람 주어라서 그럴듯해 보입니다. 이를 걸러내려면 앞 문장의 'its master handled'를 근거로 실제 행위자를 추적해야 하므로, 형태만 보는 수준을 넘는 판단이 필요합니다. 다만 A와 B는 무생물 주어라서 쉽게 제거되므로, hard 난이도로서는 하한선에 가깝습니다.

problem.passage:
In the 1960s, glaciologists working on Greenland's ice sheet began extracting long cylinders of ancient ice, but the samples often fractured during transport. Examining the cracked cores under polarized light at a laboratory in Copenhagen, ______ the fractures followed layers of volcanic ash trapped in the ice, a discovery that later allowed researchers to date eruptions with remarkable precision.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the 1960s, glaciologists working on Greenland's ice sheet began extracting long cylinders of ancient ice, but the samples often fractured during transport. Examining the cracked cores under polarized light at a laboratory in Copenhagen, ______ the fractures followed layers of volcanic ash trapped in the ice, a discovery that later allowed researchers to date eruptions with remarkable precision.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the polarized light revealed to physicist Willi Dansgaard that
the Greenland ice sheet showed physicist Willi Dansgaard that
physicist Willi Dansgaard noticed that
the ice samples' fractures made it clear to physicist Willi Dansgaard that
problem.explanation:
문두 분사구 'Examining the cracked cores...'에서 '살펴보는' 행위를 하는 주체는 사람이어야 하고, 이 주체가 주절의 주어로 바로 와야 한다. C는 physicist Willi Dansgaard를 주어로 두어 수식 관계가 올바르다(정답).
A: 분사구 안에서 가장 가까운 무생물 명사인 polarized light를 주어로 삼았기 때문에 빛이 코어를 살펴본 것처럼 읽힌다. Dansgaard는 to의 목적어로 밀려나 있다.
B: 첫 문장에 배경으로 나온 Greenland's ice sheet를 주어로 삼아 빙상이 실험실에서 코어를 관찰한 셈이 되어 버린다.
D: fractures도 코어와 관련된 대상이라 행위자처럼 보이기 쉽지만, 균열은 무언가를 관찰할 수 없다. 이 역시 현수 수식어 오류다.
problem.explanationEn:
The sentence begins with the participial phrase "Examining the cracked cores under polarized light...". A modifier like this describes whatever noun comes right after the comma, so the subject of the main clause must be the person who did the examining. Choice C puts physicist Willi Dansgaard in that position, so the modifier correctly describes him. C is the correct answer.
A: This choice makes "the polarized light" the subject. That is the inanimate noun closest to the modifier, but light can't examine cores. Dansgaard only appears as the object of "to."
B: This choice makes "the Greenland ice sheet," a background noun from the first sentence, the subject. That would mean the ice sheet examined cores in a Copenhagen lab.
D: This choice makes "the ice samples' fractures" the subject. Fractures are closely related to the cores, so they can look like a reasonable subject, but fractures can't examine anything. The modifier is still dangling.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구 'Examining the cracked cores...'의 행위자는 사람(Dansgaard)이어야 하며, C만 주절 주어로 이를 둔다. A(polarized light, 분사구 내 인접 무생물), B(배경 명사 Greenland ice sheet), D(fractures, 문법적으로 완결되나 의미상 관찰 불가)가 각각 레시피 역할을 수행. 세 오답 모두 문법적으로 완전한 절을 이루어 단순 형태 매칭이 아닌 의미상 행위자 추적을 요구함. Dansgaard가 코펜하겐 기반 그린란드 빙하코어 연구자였다는 배경은 사실과 부합하며, 균열-화산재 층 서사는 구성된 내용이나 명백한 사실 오류는 아님. 해설은 정답·오답 근거를 정확히 서술.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 옳고, 레시피 다섯 항목도 모두 충족한다. 다만 사람인 선택지는 C 하나뿐이고 A, B, D는 모두 무생물(빛, 빙상, 균열)이라서, '사람이 살펴본다'는 점만 확인하면 바로 풀린다. 의미상 행위자를 추적하는 단계가 따로 필요 없는 전형적인 medium 수준의 현수 수식어 문항이다. hard 문항이 되려면 그럴듯한 사람 명사나 집단 명사를 함정으로 두어야 한다. 사실관계: Dansgaard가 덴마크 물리학자이자 빙하코어 연구자인 것은 맞다. 다만 균열이 화산재 층을 따라 났다는 세부 내용은 확인할 수 없는 각색으로 보인다.

problem.passage:
In her 1962 field notes, marine biologist Ruth Okafor recorded what she saw on her first morning at the tidal pools near Accra: "The water retreats, the anemones close, and the crabs scatter into crevices." Months later, recounting the same scene in a lecture, she explained that by the time she arrived, the water had retreated, the anemones had closed, and the crabs ______ into crevices before she could even unpack her equipment.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In her 1962 field notes, marine biologist Ruth Okafor recorded what she saw on her first morning at the tidal pools near Accra: "The water retreats, the anemones close, and the crabs scatter into crevices." Months later, recounting the same scene in a lecture, she explained that by the time she arrived, the water had retreated, the anemones had closed, and the crabs ______ into crevices before she could even unpack her equipment.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: scatter
having scattered
would scatter
had scattered
problem.explanation: 정답 D. 빈칸은 따옴표 안의 직접 인용이 아니라 'she explained that ~' 뒤의 간접 화법이다. 'by the time she arrived'로 정해진 과거 시점보다 먼저 끝난 일을 말하고, 'had retreated, had closed'와 병렬을 이루므로 과거완료 'had scattered'가 맞다. A: 인용문 속 현재형(scatter)을 그대로 가져왔다. 간접 화법의 과거 시제 틀과 맞지 않는다. B: 분사 'having scattered'로는 'the crabs'를 주어로 하는 절이 완성되지 않고, 앞의 두 정형 동사와 병렬도 깨진다. C: 'before she could'의 조동사 과거형과는 형태가 비슷하지만, 'would scatter'는 이후에 일어날 일을 뜻한다. 그래서 도착 전에 이미 끝난 일이라는 전체 문맥과 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: The answer is D. The blank isn't part of the direct quotation. It sits in reported speech after "she explained that." The phrase "by the time she arrived" sets a past moment, and the crabs scattered before that moment. The blank also completes a series with "had retreated" and "had closed." So the past perfect "had scattered" is correct. A copies the present tense from the quotation, but that tense doesn't fit the past-tense reported speech. B uses a participle, so "the crabs" never gets a finite verb, and the parallel series breaks. C looks like it matches "could" in the nearby clause, but "would scatter" points to something that happens later. That contradicts the idea that the scattering was already finished when she arrived.

which: direct vs. indirect speech frame distinction
parallel structure across three coordinated clauses with 'by the time' past-perfect anchoring
hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산: 'she explained that by the time she arrived' 간접화법 과거 틀 + 'had retreated, had closed'와 병렬 → 'had scattered' 유일하게 적합. A는 인용문의 현재형을 그대로 옮긴 함정(체크리스트 3은 '인용문 시제를 간접화법에 잘못 적용한 오답'으로 기능적으로 충족), B는 병렬 중 하나만 비정형, C는 'before she could'와 국소적으로 어울리지만 선후관계 역전. 해설에 모순·오계산 없음. 직접 인용과 간접 화법의 시제 전환을 문맥 전체에서 추적해야 하므로 medium 초과.

advisory.note: 인용문의 현재형과 간접화법의 과거완료 병렬을 구분해야 하므로 문맥 전체에 걸친 시제 판단이 필요함. 'Ruth Okafor'는 가상 인물로 보이나 실존 주장으로 쓰인 것은 아님. 'by the time ... before she could even unpack'은 시점 표현이 겹쳐 다소 중복되지만 문법 오류는 아님.

problem.passage:
In the 1930s, the Hopi weaving cooperatives of northern Arizona attracted the attention of several museum curators, but it was the ethnobotanist Lucille Kaneshiro whose fieldwork proved most lasting. Having spent three winters recording which desert plants the weavers boiled to produce their yellows and rusts, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the 1930s, the Hopi weaving cooperatives of northern Arizona attracted the attention of several museum curators, but it was the ethnobotanist Lucille Kaneshiro whose fieldwork proved most lasting. Having spent three winters recording which desert plants the weavers boiled to produce their yellows and rusts, ______
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Kaneshiro compiled a dye catalog that conservators still consult when restoring faded textiles.
a dye catalog compiled by Kaneshiro is still consulted by conservators when restoring faded textiles.
the cooperatives' textiles were documented by Kaneshiro in a dye catalog that conservators still consult.
conservators still consult the dye catalog that Kaneshiro compiled when restoring faded textiles.
problem.explanation: 정답 A. 'Having spent three winters recording...'라는 분사구의 의미상 주어는 겨울 세 번을 들여 식물을 기록한 사람, 즉 민족식물학자 Kaneshiro이다. 따라서 분사구 바로 뒤 주절의 주어는 Kaneshiro여야 한다. B는 분사구 내용과 가장 가까운 무생물 명사인 'a dye catalog'를 주어로 두었다. 카탈로그가 겨울을 보내며 기록할 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어가 된다. C는 지문 앞부분의 배경 명사인 협동조합의 직물(the cooperatives' textiles)을 주어로 두었다. Kaneshiro가 by구에 들어가 있어 의미는 비슷해 보이지만, 문법상 기록한 주체가 직물이 되어 버린다. D는 같은 사람 명사이지만 행위자가 아닌 'conservators'를 주어로 두었다. 사람이라 그럴듯해 보이지만 세 겨울 동안 기록한 사람은 보존 전문가가 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The answer is A. The opening phrase "Having spent three winters recording..." has to describe the person who did that recording, and that person is the ethnobotanist Kaneshiro. So Kaneshiro must be the subject that comes right after the comma. B makes "a dye catalog" the subject. It's the object most closely tied to the phrase, but a catalog can't spend winters recording plants, so the modifier dangles. C makes "the cooperatives' textiles," a noun from the background part of the passage, the subject. Kaneshiro only shows up in a "by" phrase, so grammatically the textiles end up doing the recording. D picks "conservators." They're people, so the choice sounds reasonable, but they aren't the ones who did the fieldwork.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A만 분사구 'Having spent three winters recording...'의 의미상 주어(Kaneshiro)를 주절 주어로 둠. B(catalog), C(textiles), D(conservators)는 모두 현수수식. 앞 문장의 분열문(it was ... Kaneshiro whose fieldwork)과 분사구 내 'the weavers', 사람 명사 'conservators' 등이 추적 부담을 더해 medium 이상. 오답 B가 엄밀한 '인접 명사' 오류 유도는 아니며(분사구 내 weavers를 쓴 오답 없음) 전형적 '산출물 주어' 오답에 가깝다는 점만 참고.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 맞다. 기록한 행위자인 Kaneshiro를 주절의 주어로 둔 선택지는 A뿐이다. 다만 전형적인 medium 수준의 현수 수식어 문항이다. B·C는 수동태와 by구 때문에 오답이 쉽게 드러나고, D의 conservators는 분명히 행위자가 아니다. B는 지문 속 인접 명사(weavers/plants)를 이용한 일치 오류가 아니므로 3번 항목을 충족하지 못한다. 행위자를 추적하는 단계도 짧고, 문장 길이 외에 추가로 요구되는 사고가 없다.

problem.passage:
In 1929, botanist Ynes Mexia began a two-year expedition up the Amazon, traveling much of the way by canoe. Writing to a friend from a riverside camp, she described a routine that rarely varied: "Each morning I pack my plant presses, ______ the riverbanks for unfamiliar species, and dry the day's specimens over a small fire before dark." That routine produced more than 65,000 specimens over her career.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In 1929, botanist Ynes Mexia began a two-year expedition up the Amazon, traveling much of the way by canoe. Writing to a friend from a riverside camp, she described a routine that rarely varied: "Each morning I pack my plant presses, ______ the riverbanks for unfamiliar species, and dry the day's specimens over a small fire before dark." That routine produced more than 65,000 specimens over her career.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: scanned
scanning
had scanned
scan
problem.explanation:
정답 D(scan). 빈칸은 인용문 속 병렬 동사 나열 "I pack ..., ______ ..., and dry ..."의 두 번째 항목이다. 인용문은 날마다 반복되는 습관을 단순현재(pack, dry)로 말하므로 빈칸도 단순현재 scan이어야 시제와 형태가 모두 맞는다.
A(scanned): 지문 바깥의 서술(began, described)은 과거 시제이지만, 인용문 안의 시제는 Mexia가 직접 쓴 말 그대로 유지된다. 따옴표 안에서 과거형을 쓰면 pack, dry와 어긋난다.
B(scanning): 시제를 피하려는 선택이지만, 분사가 들어가면 서술어 세 개가 대등하게 이어지는 병렬 구조에서 한 항목만 형태가 달라진다.
C(had scanned): 'described'라는 과거 시점보다 앞선 일이라고 보면 주절과는 어울리는 듯하지만, 인용문 속의 현재형 습관 서술과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is D (scan). The blank is the second item in a parallel series of verbs inside the quotation: "I pack ..., ______ ..., and dry ...." Mexia describes a daily habit in the simple present (pack, dry), so the blank also needs the simple present, scan, to match in both tense and form.
A (scanned): The narration outside the quotation is in the past tense (began, described). But words inside quotation marks keep Mexia's own tense. A past-tense verb would clash with pack and dry.
B (scanning): This avoids choosing a tense, but a participle makes one item look different from the others in a series of three matching verbs. That breaks the parallel structure.
C (had scanned): Past perfect might seem to fit if you think of the action as happening before "described" in the outer sentence. It doesn't match the present-tense habit described inside the quotation, though.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D(scan)는 인용문 내 병렬 서술어 pack/dry와 형태·시제가 일치하므로 옳다. 해설은 각 오답을 체크리스트 역할대로 설명하며 모순 없음. 지문 바깥의 과거 서술(began, described)과 인용문 내부 현재 습관 서술을 구분해야 하므로 단순 병렬 문항보다 추가 판단이 요구된다. 다만 오답 C(had scanned)의 '국소적 타당성'은 다소 약해 사실상 시제 오류 변형에 가깝고, 빈칸 양옆에 pack/dry가 인접해 있어 난이도 상승폭은 제한적이다. 사실 관계: Mexia의 1929년 아마존 탐사·카누 이동·평생 표본 수(약 145,000점 이상, '65,000 이상'은 참)는 오류 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 맞다. pack, ___, and dry가 병렬로 놓여 있어 단순현재가 바로 정해진다. 바깥 서술의 과거 시제(began, described)가 함정 구실을 하긴 하지만 병렬 동사 pack/dry가 바로 옆에 있어서 국소적 단서만으로 풀린다. 따라서 문맥 전체를 따져야 하는 hard 수준의 시제 판단에는 이르지 못하고 전형적인 medium 병렬 문항에 가깝다. 인용문은 실존 인물 Mexia의 말처럼 쓰였지만 실제 출처 없이 지어낸 것으로 보이니 주의가 필요하다. Mexia의 아마존 탐사(1929~1931년, 카누 이동)와 관련된 사실 서술에는 문제가 없다. 다만 일반적으로 알려진 평생 채집량은 약 145,000점이어서 'more than 65,000'은 틀린 말은 아니어도 크게 낮춰 잡은 수치다.

problem.passage:
In the 1950s, the Hopi village of Hotevilla in northern Arizona was the site of a long-running dispute over traditional farming rights. Having spent nearly two decades recording the village's oral histories and comparing them with federal land surveys, ______ in a 2009 study that the dispute's roots lay in an 1890s allotment policy rather than in disagreements among clans.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the 1950s, the Hopi village of Hotevilla in northern Arizona was the site of a long-running dispute over traditional farming rights. Having spent nearly two decades recording the village's oral histories and comparing them with federal land surveys, ______ in a 2009 study that the dispute's roots lay in an 1890s allotment policy rather than in disagreements among clans.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the federal surveys' inconsistencies, as anthropologist Mara Velez showed, revealed
Hotevilla's farming dispute was traced by anthropologist Mara Velez
the oral histories collected by anthropologist Mara Velez's assistant demonstrated
anthropologist Mara Velez argued
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 도입 분사구 "Having spent nearly two decades recording... and comparing..."의 의미상 주어는 기록·비교라는 행위를 한 사람이어야 하므로, 그 행위자인 인류학자 Mara Velez가 주절 주어로 바로 와야 한다. 또 "argued ... that ..."이 뒤의 that절과 자연스럽게 이어진다.
A: 분사구 바로 앞에 나오는 무생물 명사(federal surveys)를 주어로 삼았다. 조사(surveys)가 20년 동안 기록 작업을 할 수는 없으므로 수식어가 엉뚱한 대상을 꾸미게 된다. Velez는 삽입구 안에 갇혀 주어 자리에 오지 못한다.
B: 첫 문장의 배경 명사(Hotevilla의 분쟁)를 주어로 삼았다. 분쟁이 기록 작업을 했다는 뜻이 되고, 수동태 뒤에 "in a 2009 study that..."이 붙으면 구조도 어색해진다.
C: Velez와 비슷한 다른 인물(조수)을 끌어들이고, 정작 주어는 oral histories로 두었다. 구술 기록이 20년간 기록 작업을 할 수는 없으므로 행위자가 일치하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, D: The opening phrase "Having spent nearly two decades recording... and comparing..." describes actions only a person could carry out. The person who did them is the anthropologist, Mara Velez, so she has to be the subject that comes right after the comma. "Argued ... that ..." also connects smoothly to the that-clause that follows.
A: This makes "the federal surveys' inconsistencies" the subject. That's the inanimate noun most closely tied to the modifier, but inconsistencies can't spend decades recording histories. Velez ends up buried in a parenthetical phrase instead of serving as the subject.
B: This makes the background noun from the first sentence, the farming dispute, the subject. That would mean the dispute did the recording. The passive verb also doesn't fit with "in a 2009 study that...".
C: This brings in a similar-sounding person, the assistant, but the actual subject is "the oral histories." Histories can't do the recording, so the modifier still doesn't match its doer.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 도입 분사구 "Having spent... recording... and comparing..."의 행위자는 사람(Velez)이어야 하므로 D만 주절 주어로 적합. A(inconsistencies, Velez는 삽입구), B(dispute, Velez는 수동태 by-구), C(oral histories, Velez의 조수는 수식어 내부)는 모두 Velez 이름을 포함해 주어처럼 보이게 유도하지만 실제 주어는 비행위자 명사로 dangling 발생. B는 "was traced ... in a 2009 study that..." 구조도 부자연스러움. 해설에서 A의 주어를 "federal surveys"로 요약한 점은 엄밀히는 "inconsistencies"이지만 논지에 영향 없음. 오답 세 개 모두에 Velez 이름이 포함되어 단순 이름 탐색이 아닌 실제 주어 추적을 요구하므로 medium 이상. Hotevilla는 실제 Hopi 마을이고 연구자·연구는 가상 설정으로 사실 오류로 보기 어려움.

advisory.note: 전형적인 현수 수식어 문항이다. 사람 행위자를 주어로 둔 선택지가 D 하나뿐이어서 즉시 정답이 가려진다. A와 C는 무생물 주어, B는 수동태라 쉽게 소거된다. 난이도는 지문 길이에서 오며, 의미상 행위자를 추적하는 깊이 있는 사고는 필요하지 않다.

problem.passage:
Ecologists studying plant defenses have proposed the resource availability hypothesis: plants that grow in nutrient-poor soils, where replacing lost leaf tissue is slow and costly, should invest more heavily in chemical defenses against herbivores than plants growing in nutrient-rich soils, where lost tissue can be regrown quickly. Researcher Ana Lindqvist examined two populations of the same shrub species in Sweden. One population grows on thin, nitrogen-depleted granite outcrops; the other grows a few kilometers away in a fertile river valley. Both populations are browsed by the same moth larvae at similar rates. If the resource availability hypothesis is correct, Lindqvist should expect that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Ecologists studying plant defenses have proposed the resource availability hypothesis: plants that grow in nutrient-poor soils, where replacing lost leaf tissue is slow and costly, should invest more heavily in chemical defenses against herbivores than plants growing in nutrient-rich soils, where lost tissue can be regrown quickly. Researcher Ana Lindqvist examined two populations of the same shrub species in Sweden. One population grows on thin, nitrogen-depleted granite outcrops; the other grows a few kilometers away in a fertile river valley. Both populations are browsed by the same moth larvae at similar rates. If the resource availability hypothesis is correct, Lindqvist should expect that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: shrubs on the granite outcrops will have leaves containing higher concentrations of defensive compounds than will shrubs in the river valley.

shrubs in the river valley will have leaves containing higher concentrations of defensive compounds than will shrubs on the granite outcrops, since they have more nutrients available to produce such compounds.
shrubs whose leaves contain high concentrations of defensive compounds will, over time, deplete the nitrogen in the soil around them more than other shrubs do.
the two populations will differ in their defensive chemistry mainly because the moth larvae in each location have adapted to different local conditions.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 이 가설은 영양이 부족한 토양일수록 잎을 다시 키우는 비용이 크기 때문에 화학적 방어에 더 많이 투자한다고 본다. 질소가 고갈된 화강암 지대의 관목은 이 '영양이 부족한' 조건에 해당하므로, 잎 속 방어 물질의 농도가 더 높을 것으로 예측된다.
B(관계 방향 뒤집기): '영양이 많으면 방어 물질을 더 많이 만들 수 있다'는 직관에 기대어, 이론과 정반대 방향의 결론을 내린다.
C(원인과 결과 뒤바꾸기): 이론에서 토양 영양 상태는 원인이고 방어 투자는 결과인데, C는 방어 물질이 토양을 고갈시킨다고 보아 인과 방향을 거꾸로 세운다.
D(이론과 무관한 제3의 요인): 차이의 원인을 유충의 지역 적응으로 돌리는데, 이는 이 가설과 관계없는 요인이다. 게다가 지문은 두 개체군이 같은 유충에게 비슷한 비율로 먹힌다고 밝혀 이런 설명을 미리 배제한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, A: The hypothesis says that plants in nutrient-poor soils, where regrowing lost leaves is costly, should invest more in chemical defenses. The shrubs on the nitrogen-depleted granite outcrops fit this nutrient-poor condition, so they should have higher concentrations of defensive compounds in their leaves.
B reverses the relationship. It relies on the intuition that having more nutrients means a plant can make more defenses, which is the opposite of what the hypothesis predicts.
C swaps cause and effect. In the theory, soil nutrient level is the cause and defense investment is the effect. C claims instead that defensive compounds deplete the soil.
D brings in a third factor that the hypothesis doesn't address: local adaptation by the larvae. The passage also says the same larvae browse both populations at similar rates, which rules out this explanation.

hardJudge.note: 가설(영양 부족 → 방어 투자 증가)이 명시되어 있고, 질소 고갈 화강암 지대 = 영양 부족 조건으로 매핑하면 A가 유일하게 방향을 유지한 예측임. B는 방향 뒤집기, C는 인과 역전, D는 가설과 무관한 제3요인이며 '같은 유충·비슷한 섭식률'이라는 통제 조건과 충돌하므로 배제됨. 해설은 정답·오답 논리를 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 다만 정답 A가 B·D보다 짧고 단순하며 B가 'since...'로 근거를 덧붙여 과잉 설명 티가 나는 점은 경미한 단서 노출 가능성 있음. 난이도는 매핑이 비교적 직접적('nitrogen-depleted'→'nutrient-poor')이어서 hard 중 하위권에 해당하나, 통제 조건을 활용한 D 배제와 방향 유지 판단이 요구되어 medium 전형 이상으로 판정.

advisory.note: 이론을 사례에 그대로 대응시키기만 하면 되는 문항이다(질소 고갈 = 영양 부족 → 방어 물질 증가). 정답 A는 지문의 가설 문장을 바꿔 말한 수준이다. B는 이유 문구까지 붙어 있어 오답임이 쉽게 드러나고, C·D는 이론의 범위를 벗어난 것이 분명하다. 대응시키는 단계가 한 번뿐이고 함정도 약해서 전형적인 medium 수준이며 hard에는 미달한다.

problem.passage:
Ecologist Mireille Okafor studied four populations of a freshwater snail living in ponds that differ in the density of crayfish, the snail's main predator. Okafor hypothesizes that snails in high-predation ponds invest more in shell thickness at the cost of reproduction, so that wherever crayfish are denser, snails should have thicker shells and lay fewer eggs per clutch.

Pond | Crayfish per m² | Mean shell thickness (mm) | Mean eggs per clutch
Alder | 0.4 | 0.31 | 58
Birch | 1.1 | 0.42 | 47
Cedar | 2.7 | 0.39 | 36
Dogwood | 3.5 | 0.55 | 29

If Okafor's hypothesis is correct in its full form, the data indicate that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
Ecologist Mireille Okafor studied four populations of a freshwater snail living in ponds that differ in the density of crayfish, the snail's main predator. Okafor hypothesizes that snails in high-predation ponds invest more in shell thickness at the cost of reproduction, so that wherever crayfish are denser, snails should have thicker shells and lay fewer eggs per clutch.

Pond | Crayfish per m² | Mean shell thickness (mm) | Mean eggs per clutch
Alder | 0.4 | 0.31 | 58
Birch | 1.1 | 0.42 | 47
Cedar | 2.7 | 0.39 | 36
Dogwood | 3.5 | 0.55 | 29

If Okafor's hypothesis is correct in its full form, the data indicate that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the Cedar population departs from the predicted pattern, since its snails lay fewer eggs than Birch snails do but do not have thicker shells than Birch snails have.
the hypothesis is fully supported, since egg numbers fall steadily as crayfish density rises from Alder to Dogwood.
the Dogwood population should show both the thickest shells and the smallest clutches, since it has the highest crayfish density of the four ponds.
the Birch population departs from the predicted pattern, since its snails have thicker shells than Alder snails have while laying fewer eggs per clutch.
problem.explanation: 가설은 포식자 밀도가 높을수록 껍데기는 두꺼워지고 알 수는 줄어든다고 예측한다. 포식자 밀도는 Birch(1.1)보다 Cedar(2.7)가 높으므로 Cedar의 껍데기가 더 두꺼워야 하지만, 실제로는 0.39mm로 Birch(0.42mm)보다 얇다. 알 수(36 < 47)는 예측대로이므로 Cedar가 예외라는 A가 정답이다. B는 표의 알 수 열만 보고 가설의 껍데기 두께 부분을 무시했다. C는 가설만으로 예측한 내용으로, 표에서 실제로 무엇이 드러나는지 말하지 않으며 Cedar의 예외도 놓친다. D는 항목을 잘못 짝지었다. Birch는 Alder보다 껍데기가 두껍고 알이 적어 가설과 정확히 일치한다.
problem.explanationEn: The hypothesis predicts that higher crayfish density means thicker shells and fewer eggs. Cedar has a higher crayfish density than Birch (2.7 vs. 1.1 per m²), so Cedar snails should have thicker shells. Instead, their shells are thinner (0.39 mm vs. 0.42 mm). Their egg count (36 vs. 47) does follow the prediction. So Cedar is the population that breaks the pattern, which makes A correct. B looks only at the egg column and ignores the shell-thickness part of the hypothesis. C just restates what the hypothesis would predict without checking the table, and it misses the Cedar exception. D points to the wrong pond: Birch has thicker shells and fewer eggs than Alder, which is exactly what the hypothesis predicts.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 밀도순 Alder<Birch<Cedar<Dogwood. 껍데기 0.31→0.42→0.39→0.55로 Cedar가 Birch보다 얇음(0.39<0.42), 알 수 58→47→36→29로 단조 감소. 가설의 두 예측 중 껍데기 부분에서 Cedar만 이탈 → A 정답. B는 알 수 열만(표 단일 자료), C는 가설 텍스트만으로 예측, D는 Alder–Birch 쌍을 잘못 연결(실제로 가설과 일치). 해설 수치·논리 일치. 사소한 점: 스템 "If Okafor's hypothesis is correct in its full form, the data indicate that…"는 '가설을 온전히 적용하면'의 의미로 읽히나 약간 어색함(판정에는 영향 없음). 두 열을 모두 대조해 예외를 찾아야 하므로 medium 이상.

advisory.note: 검산 결과: 포식자 밀도는 Cedar(2.7)가 Birch(1.1)보다 높은데 껍데기는 Cedar 0.39mm로 Birch 0.42mm보다 얇습니다. 알 수(36<47)는 예측과 맞으므로 A가 정답입니다. 가설의 두 변수(껍데기 두께, 알 수)를 모두 확인해야 예외를 찾을 수 있어 medium보다 한 단계 더 사고를 요구합니다. 오답 구성: B는 시각 자료만 사용(알 수 열), C는 텍스트만 사용, D는 Birch–Alder 비교를 잘못 연결한 것입니다. 사소한 점: 문두 'If Okafor's hypothesis is correct in its full form, the data indicate that'는 다소 어색합니다. 전제가 '가설이 옳다면'인데 결론이 데이터의 예외를 가리키기 때문입니다. 다만 정답 판정에는 영향이 없습니다.

problem.passage:
Ecologists studying freshwater snails have proposed that the thickness of a snail's shell reflects the predation pressure its population has experienced over many generations: where shell-crushing predators such as crayfish are abundant, snails that invest more calcium in thicker shells survive to reproduce, so populations facing heavier predation evolve thicker shells. Building thick shells is costly, however, so where crushing predators are scarce, thinner-shelled snails, which can devote more resources to growth and reproduction, tend to prevail. Researcher Ana Lindqvist sampled snails of a single species from two connected lakes with similar water chemistry and calcium availability. Crayfish have been common in Lake Ormsby for centuries, whereas Lake Vell has had almost no crayfish over the same period. If the ecologists' proposal is correct, Lindqvist should find that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Ecologists studying freshwater snails have proposed that the thickness of a snail's shell reflects the predation pressure its population has experienced over many generations: where shell-crushing predators such as crayfish are abundant, snails that invest more calcium in thicker shells survive to reproduce, so populations facing heavier predation evolve thicker shells. Building thick shells is costly, however, so where crushing predators are scarce, thinner-shelled snails, which can devote more resources to growth and reproduction, tend to prevail. Researcher Ana Lindqvist sampled snails of a single species from two connected lakes with similar water chemistry and calcium availability. Crayfish have been common in Lake Ormsby for centuries, whereas Lake Vell has had almost no crayfish over the same period. If the ecologists' proposal is correct, Lindqvist should find that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: snails from Lake Ormsby, on average, have thicker shells than snails from Lake Vell do.
snails from Lake Vell, on average, have thicker shells than snails from Lake Ormsby do, since they can afford greater investment in calcium.
the crayfish in Lake Ormsby became abundant because the lake's snails had developed thinner shells that were easier to crush.
shell thickness differs between the two lakes mainly because of differences in the calcium content of their water.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 이론에 따르면 껍데기를 부수는 포식자가 많을수록 두꺼운 껍데기가 진화한다. 가재가 수백 년간 흔했던 Ormsby 호수의 달팽이가 가재가 거의 없던 Vell 호수의 달팽이보다 껍데기가 두꺼워야 한다.
B(방향 반전): 포식자가 드문 곳에서는 비용이 큰 두꺼운 껍데기가 오히려 불리하므로 얇은 껍데기가 우세하다고 지문에 나와 있다. '자원 여유'라는 그럴듯한 논리를 덧붙였지만 이론과 반대 방향이다.
C(인과 역전): 이론은 포식 압력이 껍데기 두께를 만든다고 하지, 껍데기 두께가 포식자 수를 결정한다고 하지 않는다. 게다가 얇은 껍데기를 예측하는 것도 이론과 어긋난다.
D(제3요인): 지문은 두 호수의 수질과 칼슘 이용 가능성이 비슷하다고 밝혀 이 요인을 통제했다. 이론과 무관하고 지문 정보와도 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, A: The theory says heavier pressure from shell-crushing predators leads snails to evolve thicker shells. Crayfish have been common in Lake Ormsby for centuries and nearly absent from Lake Vell. So Ormsby snails should have thicker shells than Vell snails.
B flips the direction. The passage says thick shells are costly, so where predators are scarce, thinner shells win out. The line about affording more calcium sounds reasonable, but it goes against the theory.
C swaps cause and effect. In the theory, predation shapes shell thickness. Shells don't determine how many predators there are. C also predicts thinner shells in Ormsby, which contradicts the theory.
D brings in an outside factor. The passage says both lakes have similar water chemistry and calcium availability, which rules calcium out as the explanation. It also has nothing to do with the predation theory.

hardJudge.note: 지문에 포식 압력→껍데기 두께의 방향성 이론이 명시되고, 두 호수(Ormsby: 가재 풍부 / Vell: 가재 희소)라는 새 사례에 적용하는 구조. 정답 A는 이론 방향 그대로. B는 '자원 여유'라는 그럴듯한 근거로 방향을 반전한 함정, C는 인과 역전, D는 지문에서 통제된 제3요인(칼슘·수질 유사)으로 지문 정보와 모순. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 오답 분류도 적절. 칼슘 통제 조건을 읽고 D를 배제해야 하므로 medium을 넘는 사고를 요구. 형식·저작권·사실 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 이론을 사례에 그대로 한 번 대입하면 끝나는 문항이다. 오답 B는 지문 내용과 정면으로 어긋나고, C와 D도 쉽게 제거되므로 전형적인 medium 수준에 해당한다. 함정이 약하고 다른 자료와 결합하거나 반례를 고려할 필요도 없어 hard 기준에는 미달한다.

problem.passage:
Ecologist Mariela Ostrovsky studied four alpine lakes in which a nonnative trout had been stocked decades ago. She recorded the trout density and the number of native frog egg masses found per survey in each lake.

Lake | Trout per hectare | Frog egg masses per survey
Crestline | 0 | 41
Larkspur | 12 | 38
Hollin | 35 | 9
Wexmere | 60 | 7

Ostrovsky hypothesizes that trout suppress frog breeding only after their density passes a threshold at which they begin systematically patrolling the shallow margins where frogs lay eggs; below that threshold, trout remain mostly in deep water and have little effect. If her hypothesis is correct, the data suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus:
Ecologist Mariela Ostrovsky studied four alpine lakes in which a nonnative trout had been stocked decades ago. She recorded the trout density and the number of native frog egg masses found per survey in each lake.

Lake | Trout per hectare | Frog egg masses per survey
Crestline | 0 | 41
Larkspur | 12 | 38
Hollin | 35 | 9
Wexmere | 60 | 7

Ostrovsky hypothesizes that trout suppress frog breeding only after their density passes a threshold at which they begin systematically patrolling the shallow margins where frogs lay eggs; below that threshold, trout remain mostly in deep water and have little effect. If her hypothesis is correct, the data suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the threshold density at which trout begin patrolling shallow margins lies somewhere above 12 but no higher than 35 trout per hectare.
frog breeding declines steadily as trout density increases, with each additional trout per hectare reducing the number of egg masses.
removing all trout from Wexmere would be expected to restore frog egg masses to roughly the level observed at Crestline.
the threshold density at which trout begin patrolling shallow margins lies somewhere above 35 but no higher than 60 trout per hectare.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 가설에 따르면 임계 밀도 이하에서는 영향이 거의 없고, 넘으면 급감한다. 표에서 12마리(Larkspur, 38)는 0마리(41)와 거의 같으므로 임계값 이하이고, 35마리(Hollin, 9)에서 급감했으므로 이미 임계값을 넘었다. 따라서 임계값은 12 초과 35 이하이다.
B: 표만 보고 '송어가 많을수록 알 덩어리가 적다'는 단조 경향만 읽은 결론으로, 임계값 가설(문턱 아래에서는 영향 거의 없음)을 무시했고 0→12 구간의 미미한 변화와도 맞지 않는다.
C: 가설 문장만 보고 '송어가 원인이니 제거하면 회복된다'고 확장한 결론으로, 자료는 제거 실험을 다루지 않으며 회복 여부를 보여 주지 않는다.
D: 급감 지점을 Hollin–Wexmere(35→60) 구간으로 잘못 짝지었다. 실제 급감은 Larkspur–Hollin 사이에서 일어났고, 35에서 이미 9로 낮다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The hypothesis says trout have little effect below a threshold density and suppress frog breeding sharply above it. At 12 trout per hectare (Larkspur, 38 egg masses), the count is close to the trout-free Crestline value (41), so 12 is below the threshold. At 35 (Hollin, 9 egg masses), breeding has already collapsed, so the threshold has been passed. That puts the threshold above 12 and no higher than 35.
B reads only the overall downward trend in the table and ignores the threshold hypothesis. It also doesn't fit the tiny change between 0 and 12 trout per hectare.
C builds on the hypothesis alone (trout cause the decline, so removing them should fix it). But the data never test removing trout, so they can't show that frogs would recover.
D pairs up the wrong rows. The sharp drop happens between Larkspur and Hollin, not between Hollin and Wexmere. Hollin is already low at 35 trout per hectare.

hardJudge.note: 표(0→41, 12→38, 35→9, 60→7)와 임계값 가설을 결합하면 영향이 거의 없는 구간은 0~12, 급감은 12~35 사이에서 발생하므로 임계값은 12 초과 35 이하 → A 정답 검산 일치. B는 표만 읽은 단조 감소 결론(0→12, 35→60 구간의 미미한 변화와도 불일치), C는 가설 문장만 확장한 제거·회복 추론, D는 급감 구간을 Hollin–Wexmere로 잘못 짝지은 오답으로 체크리스트 전 항목 충족. 가설의 '임계값' 개념을 구체 수치 구간에 적용해야 하며 두 자료를 모두 참조해야만 도출 가능하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구함. 해설에 모순·오계산 없음.

advisory.note: 임계값 가설을 표의 급감 구간(12→35)에 적용해 구간을 추론해야 함. D는 인접 구간 오연결 함정으로 적절함. 12에서 41→38로 약간 줄어든 것도 '영향 거의 없음'에 부합함.

problem.passage:
Medieval scribes who copied manuscripts by hand sometimes left marginal notes complaining of cold, hunger, or fatigue. Historian Lena Okafor hypothesizes that such complaints were not spontaneous outbursts but a learned convention: novice scribes, she argues, absorbed the habit from the exemplars they were assigned to copy, which already contained similar notes. If Okafor is correct, then a scribe's complaints should track the texts the scribe copied rather than the conditions the scribe worked in. Okafor's hypothesis would therefore be most strongly supported if it were found that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Medieval scribes who copied manuscripts by hand sometimes left marginal notes complaining of cold, hunger, or fatigue. Historian Lena Okafor hypothesizes that such complaints were not spontaneous outbursts but a learned convention: novice scribes, she argues, absorbed the habit from the exemplars they were assigned to copy, which already contained similar notes. If Okafor is correct, then a scribe's complaints should track the texts the scribe copied rather than the conditions the scribe worked in. Okafor's hypothesis would therefore be most strongly supported if it were found that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: scribes working in the same unheated scriptorium during the same winter added complaints only when copying from exemplars that already contained complaints.
complaints about cold appear far more often in manuscripts copied during winter months than in those copied during summer months.
many monasteries required novice scribes to copy texts for several years before they were permitted to compose original writing.
some marginal complaints were written in a different ink from the main text, suggesting they were added after copying was finished.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 같은 필사실, 같은 겨울이라는 동일한 환경 조건에서도 원본(exemplar)에 불평이 이미 있을 때만 필사자가 불평을 덧붙였다면, 불평은 환경이 아니라 베끼는 텍스트를 따른다는 뜻이 된다. 이는 가설의 핵심 예측을 직접 충족한다.
B: 겨울에 추위 불평이 더 많다는 것은 불평이 실제 작업 환경을 반영한다는 뜻이므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. 가설과 반대 방향의 사실을 지지 근거처럼 제시한 함정이다.
C: 수습 필사자가 오랜 기간 필사만 했다는 것은 관습을 '배울' 기회가 있었다는 배경일 뿐, 불평이 원본을 따랐는지는 보여 주지 않는다. 결론을 지지하는 것처럼 위장한 배경 정보다.
D: 잉크가 다르다는 것은 불평이 '언제' 쓰였는지에 관한 것이지, 불평이 원본에서 배운 관습인지 실제 조건에 대한 반응인지는 구분해 주지 않는다. 표면적으로만 관련된 사실이다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The scribes worked in the same unheated scriptorium during the same winter, so their working conditions were the same. If they still added complaints only when the exemplar already had them, then the complaints followed the text being copied, not the conditions. That is exactly what Okafor's hypothesis predicts, so this fact supports it directly.
B: If complaints about cold show up more often in winter, they reflect real working conditions. That cuts against the hypothesis. It is evidence pointing the opposite way, presented as if it were support.
C: Years of copying before writing anything original tells you novices had a chance to pick up habits. It is only background, though. It doesn't show that their complaints actually followed their exemplars.
D: A different ink tells you when the complaints were written. It doesn't tell you whether they were a learned convention or a reaction to real hardship. It looks relevant but doesn't test the hypothesis.

hardJudge.note: 가설→예측(텍스트 추적 vs 환경 추적)이 명시되고, A는 환경을 통제한 상태에서 텍스트 변수만 달라지는 사례로 예측을 직접 충족. B는 반대 방향(환경 반영) 함정, C는 배경 정보, D는 시점 정보로 무관. 해설의 각 선택지 분석이 논리적으로 일관되며 모순 없음. 답 A 확정 가능하고 가상의 역사가(Okafor) 설정으로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: A는 환경 조건을 고정하고 원본 텍스트만 달리하는 통제 비교라서, 이를 알아보는 데 추가 사고가 필요하다. B는 반대 방향 함정, C·D는 관련 있어 보이지만 무관한 사실이다. 다만 지문이 예측('track the texts... rather than the conditions')을 명시하고 있어 난이도는 hard 하한선 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Medieval scribes copying manuscripts by hand often introduced errors, and textual scholars use these errors to reconstruct how copies descended from one another. Historian Lena Marrow has proposed that two fourteenth-century copies of a Latin herbal, one held in Bruges and one in Ghent, were not copied from each other but were both copied independently from a single lost exemplar. Under her hypothesis, any distinctive error that originated in the lost exemplar should appear in both copies, whereas errors a scribe introduced while making one copy should appear only in that copy. Marrow's hypothesis would therefore be most directly undermined if it were found that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Medieval scribes copying manuscripts by hand often introduced errors, and textual scholars use these errors to reconstruct how copies descended from one another. Historian Lena Marrow has proposed that two fourteenth-century copies of a Latin herbal, one held in Bruges and one in Ghent, were not copied from each other but were both copied independently from a single lost exemplar. Under her hypothesis, any distinctive error that originated in the lost exemplar should appear in both copies, whereas errors a scribe introduced while making one copy should appear only in that copy. Marrow's hypothesis would therefore be most directly undermined if it were found that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the Ghent copy contains every distinctive error found in the Bruges copy, along with several additional errors that appear in no other known manuscript, while the Bruges copy contains no errors absent from the Ghent copy.
the Bruges and Ghent copies share a number of distinctive errors, including a misspelled plant name that appears in no other surviving manuscript of the herbal.
the Bruges copy was written on parchment prepared in a different workshop from the one that produced the parchment used for the Ghent copy.
fourteenth-century scribes in the region were commonly trained to copy texts from exemplars rather than from dictation, a practice that tended to reduce certain kinds of errors.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 가설은 두 사본이 서로를 베끼지 않고 각자 독립적으로 사라진 원본에서 나왔다고 본다. 그렇다면 필사자마다 자기만의 오류를 새로 만들었을 것이므로, 두 사본 모두 상대 사본에 없는 고유 오류를 가지고 있어야 한다. 그런데 Bruges 사본에는 고유 오류가 전혀 없고 그 오류가 전부 Ghent 사본에 들어 있으며, Ghent 사본에만 오류가 더 있다면, Ghent가 Bruges를 베꼈다고 보는 것이 가장 자연스럽다. 따라서 '독립적으로 필사했다'는 가설의 핵심 조건을 직접 깨뜨린다.
B(반대 방향의 사실을 약화 근거처럼 제시): 두 사본이 공유하는 독특한 오류는 원본에서 물려받았다는 설명과 잘 맞는다. 즉 가설을 약화하는 것이 아니라 오히려 뒷받침한다.
C(표면적으로만 관련 있는 사실): 양피지를 만든 공방이 달랐다는 것은 '독립성'처럼 들리지만, 원문이 어떻게 전해졌는지와는 상관이 없다.
D(배경 정보로 위장한 선택지): 당시 필사 관행에 대한 일반적인 정보일 뿐, 이 두 사본의 관계에 대해서는 아무것도 알려 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: Marrow's hypothesis says each copy came straight from the lost exemplar. If that's true, each scribe would have added some new errors of his own, so each copy should contain errors that the other copy lacks. Choice A describes a different pattern. The Bruges copy has no errors of its own, and every one of its errors also shows up in the Ghent copy, which has extra errors besides. The simplest explanation for that pattern is that the Ghent copy was copied from the Bruges copy. That directly contradicts the claim that the two copies were made independently.
B (a fact that actually supports the hypothesis, offered as if it weakened it): Distinctive errors that appear in both copies are exactly what you would expect if both inherited them from the exemplar. So B supports the hypothesis instead of undermining it.
C (sounds relevant but isn't): Parchment from different workshops may sound like a sign of independence, but it tells you nothing about which text each scribe copied from.
D (background presented as if it mattered): A general fact about how scribes were trained says nothing about how these two particular copies are related.

hardJudge.note: 가설(독립 필사)과 그에 따른 예측(각 사본에 고유 오류 존재, 공유 오류는 원본 유래)이 명확히 제시됨. A는 Bruges에 고유 오류가 전혀 없고 Ghent가 Bruges의 오류를 모두 포함하는 '상위집합' 패턴으로, 독립 필사가 아니라 Ghent가 Bruges를 베꼈음을 시사하여 가설을 직접 약화함. 엄밀히 '필사자가 오류를 전혀 내지 않았을 가능성'이 논리적으로 남지만, 지문 첫 문장(필사자들은 흔히 오류를 냄)과 선택지 간 비교에서 A가 가장 직접적인 약화 근거임은 분명함. B는 공유 오류가 원본 유래라는 가설 예측과 부합하여 오히려 지지(반대 방향 위장), C는 양피지 공방 차이로 전승 관계와 무관하나 '독립성'처럼 보이는 함정, D는 일반 배경 정보. 해설은 정답·오답 논리를 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 오류 패턴을 계통 관계로 역추론해야 하므로 medium 이상의 이론-사례 적용과 증거 충분성 판단을 요구함.

advisory.note: A는 두 사본이 독립적으로 필사됐다면 각 사본에 고유 오류가 있어야 한다는 함의를 이끌어내야 풀 수 있다. 지문은 이 함의를 직접 말하지 않는다. 그래서 단순 대조로는 풀리지 않는다. B는 방향을 뒤집은 함정이다. 실제로는 가설을 지지하지만, 오류 공유가 곧 서로 베꼈다는 뜻이라고 착각하면 약화 근거로 고르게 된다. 엄밀히 보면 Bruges 필사자가 고유 오류를 하나도 만들지 않았을 가능성도 있다. 그래도 A가 가장 직접적으로 가설을 약화한다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Bioluminescent organisms produce light through chemical reactions involving a molecule called luciferin.
- The firefly squid (Watasenia scintillans) lives off the coast of Japan and emits blue light from organs on its arms.
- The firefly squid uses its light mainly to attract mates and to camouflage itself against light from the surface above.
- The railroad worm (Phrixothrix hirtus) is a beetle larva found in South America.
- The railroad worm emits red light from its head, a color that most of its prey cannot detect.
- The railroad worm uses this red light to locate prey in the dark without being noticed.

The student wants to contrast how the two organisms use their light. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Bioluminescent organisms produce light through chemical reactions involving a molecule called luciferin.
- The firefly squid (Watasenia scintillans) lives off the coast of Japan and emits blue light from organs on its arms.
- The firefly squid uses its light mainly to attract mates and to camouflage itself against light from the surface above.
- The railroad worm (Phrixothrix hirtus) is a beetle larva found in South America.
- The railroad worm emits red light from its head, a color that most of its prey cannot detect.
- The railroad worm uses this red light to locate prey in the dark without being noticed.
problem.question: The student wants to contrast how the two organisms use their light. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the firefly squid uses its blue light mainly to attract mates and to blend in with light from above, the railroad worm uses its red light to find prey that cannot see it.
The railroad worm, a South American beetle larva, emits red light from its head, a color that most of its prey cannot detect, allowing it to hunt unnoticed.
The firefly squid lives off the coast of Japan and glows blue, while the railroad worm is a beetle larva found in South America and glows red.
Whereas the firefly squid uses its blue light to frighten away predators, the railroad worm uses its red light to find prey that cannot see it.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 두 생물의 빛 '용도'(오징어: 짝 유인·위장 / 철도벌레: 들키지 않고 먹이 찾기)를 whereas로 대조해 목표를 충족한다.
B: 철도벌레의 빛 용도만 설명하고 반딧불오징어는 빠져 있어 대조가 절반만 이루어진다.
C: 두 생물을 대조하긴 하지만 서식지와 빛의 색을 비교할 뿐, 목표인 빛의 용도는 다루지 않는다.
D: 대조 구조는 갖췄지만 '포식자를 쫓아낸다'는 노트에 없는 내용으로, 오징어의 실제 용도(짝 유인·위장)를 왜곡한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: It contrasts how each organism uses its light. The squid uses it to attract mates and blend in with light from above, and the worm uses it to find prey without being seen. The word "whereas" sets up the contrast, so the goal is met.
B: It only describes how the railroad worm uses its light. The squid is left out, so there is no contrast.
C: It does compare the two organisms, but only their habitats and light colors. It never says how either one uses its light, which is what the goal asks for.
D: It has a contrast structure, but the notes never say the squid uses its light to frighten predators. This changes the squid's actual purposes (attracting mates and camouflage).

hardJudge.note: A는 두 생물의 빛 용도를 whereas로 정확히 대조하며 노트 내용에 충실. B는 한쪽만, C는 대조 구조이나 목표(용도)가 아닌 서식지·색 비교로 purpose_scope_calibration 요구, D는 노트에 없는 내용. 오답 C가 '대조'라는 형식은 갖추되 초점이 어긋나 있어 단순 사실 선택 이상의 목적 범위 판단을 요구함. 실제 생물학적 사실(반딧불오징어 서식지·청색광, 철도벌레 적색광·남미 서식)도 정확. 다만 오답 B가 다소 쉽게 배제되어 hard 상한선은 아님.

advisory.note: 전형적인 medium 수준의 대조 문항이다. 정답 A만 '빛의 용도'를 두 생물 모두에 대해 대조하고 있어 쉽게 판별된다. C는 다른 속성(서식지·빛의 색)을 대조하고, D는 노트에 없는 내용을 넣었으며, B는 한쪽만 다룬다. 모두 표준적인 오답 유형이다. 확실성 수준 구분, 독자 배경 고려, 관계 방향 판단 같은 hard 특성은 요구되지 않는다. 노트 첫 줄(luciferin)은 정보 수 채우기용 방해 요소일 뿐이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tardigrades are microscopic animals, usually less than 1 millimeter long, found in mosses, soils, and oceans worldwide.
- When their surroundings dry out, tardigrades can enter a state called anhydrobiosis, losing nearly all their body water.
- In this dried state, some tardigrades have revived after exposure to temperatures as low as −272°C.
- In 2007, dried tardigrades carried into low Earth orbit survived direct exposure to the vacuum of space.
- Tardigrades were first described by German zoologist Johann August Ephraim Goeze in 1773.

The student wants to emphasize the range of extreme conditions that dried tardigrades can survive. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tardigrades are microscopic animals, usually less than 1 millimeter long, found in mosses, soils, and oceans worldwide.
- When their surroundings dry out, tardigrades can enter a state called anhydrobiosis, losing nearly all their body water.
- In this dried state, some tardigrades have revived after exposure to temperatures as low as −272°C.
- In 2007, dried tardigrades carried into low Earth orbit survived direct exposure to the vacuum of space.
- Tardigrades were first described by German zoologist Johann August Ephraim Goeze in 1773.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize the range of extreme conditions that dried tardigrades can survive. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In a dried state known as anhydrobiosis, tardigrades have withstood both temperatures as low as −272°C and the vacuum of space.
In 2007, dried tardigrades carried into low Earth orbit survived direct exposure to the vacuum of space.
Tardigrades, microscopic animals found in mosses, soils, and oceans worldwide, have interested scientists for centuries.
First described by Johann August Ephraim Goeze in 1773, tardigrades are usually less than 1 millimeter long.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 건조 상태의 완보동물이 견디는 극한 조건의 '범위'를 강조하는 것이다. A는 건조 상태(anhydrobiosis)를 명시하고 극저온과 우주 진공이라는 서로 다른 두 극한 조건을 함께 제시해 범위를 보여 준다.
B(지나치게 세부적): 2007년 우주 실험이라는 단일 사례만 제시하므로 '범위'가 드러나지 않는다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 완보동물에 대한 일반적 소개일 뿐 극한 조건 생존이라는 초점이 사라졌다.
D(무관한 항목): 최초 기술 연도와 몸 크기를 강조하여 목표와 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The goal is to emphasize the range of extreme conditions that dried tardigrades can survive. A names the dried state (anhydrobiosis) and pairs two very different extremes, near-absolute-zero cold and the vacuum of space. Putting them together shows a range.
B is too narrow. It gives only the single 2007 space experiment, and one condition can't show a range.
C is too broad. It's a general introduction to tardigrades and never mentions surviving extreme conditions.
D uses unrelated notes. It highlights who first described tardigrades, when, and how big they are, none of which serves the goal.

hardJudge.note: 목표가 '범위(range)'이므로 두 가지 서로 다른 극한 조건(−272°C, 우주 진공)을 건조 상태라는 공통 전제와 함께 통합한 A만이 부합. B는 단일 사례(지나치게 구체적), C는 일반 소개(지나치게 포괄적), D는 무관. 사실관계(−272°C 생존 보고, 2007 FOTON-M3 우주 노출 실험, Goeze 1773) 모두 정확. 사소한 점: 노트는 'some tardigrades'인데 A는 'tardigrades'로 일반화했으나 SAT 관행상 허용 범위. C의 'have interested scientists for centuries'는 노트에 직접 없으나 1773 기술에서 추론 가능하며 오답이므로 문제 없음. 난이도는 전형적 수준에 가깝지만 세 노트를 하나의 문장으로 종합해야 하는 점에서 medium 이상으로 판단.

advisory.note: 정답은 맞고 해설도 일관적이다. 다만 극한 조건 두 가지(극저온, 진공)를 모두 담은 선택지가 A 하나뿐이고 C와 D는 주제에서 확연히 벗어나 있다. 그래서 '범위'라는 단어만 보고 바로 풀 수 있는 전형적인 medium 수준의 문항이다. B는 단일 사례로서 매력적인 오답이지만, 실제로 종합하거나 범위를 판단하는 사고를 요구하지는 않는다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mariana Ostrowska surveyed 40 eelgrass meadows in the Baltic Sea.
- She measured sediment carbon directly and found that meadow sites stored, on average, 2.3 times as much carbon as nearby bare seabed sites.
- She also observed that meadows with more grazing snails tended to have denser eelgrass shoots.
- Ostrowska proposes that the snails may help by scraping algae off eelgrass leaves, but she notes that this explanation has not yet been tested experimentally.
- In a separate 2019 study, a different team showed that eelgrass roots release oxygen into surrounding sediment.

The student wants to present Ostrowska's finding about snails while accurately conveying how certain it is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mariana Ostrowska surveyed 40 eelgrass meadows in the Baltic Sea.
- She measured sediment carbon directly and found that meadow sites stored, on average, 2.3 times as much carbon as nearby bare seabed sites.
- She also observed that meadows with more grazing snails tended to have denser eelgrass shoots.
- Ostrowska proposes that the snails may help by scraping algae off eelgrass leaves, but she notes that this explanation has not yet been tested experimentally.
- In a separate 2019 study, a different team showed that eelgrass roots release oxygen into surrounding sediment.
problem.question: The student wants to present Ostrowska's finding about snails while accurately conveying how certain it is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ostrowska's survey of 40 Baltic meadows showed that grazing snails make eelgrass shoots denser by scraping algae off the plants' leaves.
Ostrowska's data suggest that eelgrass meadows might store somewhat more sediment carbon than bare seabed, though the snails' role in this remains uncertain.
In Ostrowska's survey, meadows with more grazing snails tended to have denser shoots, perhaps because the snails clear algae from leaves, an idea that has yet to be tested experimentally.
Ostrowska suggests that grazing snails may contribute to denser eelgrass shoots by helping release oxygen into the sediment, though this has not been confirmed.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 노트상 달팽이 결과는 '경향(tended to)'이라는 상관관계이고, 조류 제거 설명은 실험으로 검증되지 않은 가설이다. C는 이 상관관계와 가설의 잠정성을 모두 정확히 살렸다.
A: 잠정적 결과를 과장한 오답이다. 상관관계를 인과로 바꾸고("make … denser"), 검증되지 않은 메커니즘을 '보여주었다(showed)'고 단정했다.
B: 확정적 사실을 축소한 오답이다. 탄소 저장량은 직접 측정한 결과(평균 2.3배)인데 'might', 'somewhat'로 약하게 표현했고, 목표인 달팽이 결과도 제대로 제시하지 못한다.
D: 확실성 수준(may, not confirmed)은 맞지만 메커니즘을 혼동했다. 퇴적물로 산소를 방출하는 것은 2019년 다른 연구팀이 보고한 eelgrass 뿌리의 특성이지 달팽이와는 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer C: In the notes, the snail finding is a correlation (meadows with more snails "tended to" have denser shoots), and the algae-scraping explanation has not been tested experimentally. C keeps both the correlation and the tentative status of the explanation, so its level of certainty matches the notes.
A overstates a tentative result. It turns a correlation into cause and effect ("make … denser") and says the survey "showed" a mechanism that no one has tested.
B weakens a firm finding without reason. Ostrowska measured carbon directly and found 2.3 times as much, yet B hedges this with "might" and "somewhat." It also never presents the snail finding, which is what the goal asks for.
D has the right level of certainty ("may," "not confirmed") but gives the wrong mechanism. In a separate 2019 study, a different team found that eelgrass roots release oxygen into sediment. That finding has nothing to do with snails.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 직접 측정된 확정적 결과(탄소 2.3배)와 잠정적 결과(달팽이 상관관계 + 미검증 가설)가 함께 제시됨. 정답 C는 'tended to'의 상관관계와 'perhaps/yet to be tested'의 가설 지위를 정확히 보존. A는 상관→인과, 가설→'showed'로 과잉 일반화; B는 확정 측정치를 'might/somewhat'로 축소하고 달팽이 목표도 미충족; D는 2019년 별도 연구의 뿌리 산소 방출 메커니즘을 달팽이에 잘못 귀속시킨 교차 소스 혼동 오답. 인과 방향·확실성 수준·다중 메모 간 귀속을 동시에 판별해야 하므로 medium을 넘는 사고 요구. 해설은 정답 및 각 오답 사유와 정확히 일치.

advisory.note: C는 상관관계와 아직 검증되지 않은 가설이라는 점을 모두 정확히 반영한다. A는 과잉 일반화한 오답, B는 확실성을 축소한 오답이며 B는 주제에서도 벗어난다. D는 다른 연구의 메커니즘과 섞어 놓은 오답이다. B가 목표에서 벗어나 있어 쉽게 제거된다는 점은 다소 약하지만, A와 D를 가르려면 확실성 수준과 출처를 구분해야 하므로 hard로 볼 수 있다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) is a radio telescope in northern Chile.
- ALMA sits on the Chajnantor Plateau at an elevation of about 5,000 meters.
- High elevation places a telescope above much of the atmosphere's water vapor, which absorbs millimeter-wavelength signals.
- The Square Kilometre Array (SKA) Low telescope is being built in Western Australia's Murchison region.
- The Murchison site was chosen because it is extremely remote, with very little radio interference from phones, broadcasts, and other human technology.

The student wants to contrast the main reasons the two telescopes' sites were selected. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) is a radio telescope in northern Chile.
- ALMA sits on the Chajnantor Plateau at an elevation of about 5,000 meters.
- High elevation places a telescope above much of the atmosphere's water vapor, which absorbs millimeter-wavelength signals.
- The Square Kilometre Array (SKA) Low telescope is being built in Western Australia's Murchison region.
- The Murchison site was chosen because it is extremely remote, with very little radio interference from phones, broadcasts, and other human technology.
problem.question: The student wants to contrast the main reasons the two telescopes' sites were selected. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: ALMA was placed at about 5,000 meters to rise above signal-absorbing water vapor, whereas SKA-Low's Murchison site was chosen for its remoteness from human radio interference.
Located at an elevation of about 5,000 meters on Chile's Chajnantor Plateau, ALMA sits above much of the atmosphere's water vapor, which absorbs millimeter-wavelength signals.
ALMA is a radio telescope in northern Chile, while SKA-Low is being built in Western Australia's Murchison region.
ALMA's high elevation protects it from water vapor, whereas SKA-Low's remote site, also at high elevation, keeps it free from human radio interference.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: ALMA 부지 선정 이유(고도 → 수증기 회피)와 SKA-Low 부지 선정 이유(외딴 곳 → 인공 전파 간섭 적음)를 whereas로 대조하여 목표를 완전히 달성한다.
B: ALMA의 이유만 자세히 설명하고 SKA-Low는 빠져 있어 대조가 성립하지 않는다(목표의 절반만 달성).
C: 두 망원경을 모두 언급하고 대조 구조도 갖췄지만 '위치'만 비교할 뿐 부지를 선택한 '이유'는 대조하지 않는다(목표와 무관한 결합).
D: 노트에는 Murchison 부지가 고지대라는 정보가 없다. 'also at high elevation'을 덧붙여 사실을 왜곡했고, 그 결과 두 부지의 차이점도 흐려진다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice A is correct. It gives the reason each site was chosen: ALMA's high elevation keeps it above water vapor that absorbs signals, and SKA-Low's remote site keeps it away from human radio interference. The word "whereas" sets up the contrast the goal asks for.
Choice B only explains ALMA's site and never mentions SKA-Low, so it meets just half of the goal.
Choice C names both telescopes and uses a contrast structure, but it only compares where they are, not why their sites were chosen.
Choice D adds a claim that isn't in the notes, that the Murchison site is also at high elevation. That distorts the facts and weakens the contrast between the two reasons.

hardJudge.note: 노트 5개 중 ALMA 측은 2·3번 노트를 인과로 연결(고도→수증기 회피)해야 '이유'가 도출되고, SKA 측은 5번 노트에서 이유를 추출해야 하므로 다중 메모 종합이 필요하다. C는 두 망원경을 대조 구조로 제시하지만 '위치'와 '이유'의 목표 범위 차이를 판별해야 하는 매력적 오답이며, D는 노트에 없는 'also at high elevation'을 끼워넣어 대조를 흐린다. 정답 A는 whereas로 두 부지 선정 이유를 정확히 대조한다. 사실 관계(ALMA 약 5,000m Chajnantor, SKA-Low Murchison 전파 간섭 최소)도 실제와 부합. 형식 정상.

advisory.note: 전형적인 medium 수준의 대조 문항이다. 정답은 'whereas'와 '이유'를 함께 담은 유일한 선택지라서 표면적인 단서만으로도 쉽게 고를 수 있다. B는 한쪽 망원경만 다루고, C는 이유 없이 위치만 비교하며, D는 노트에 없는 정보를 덧붙여서 각각 바로 걸러진다. 따라서 목적 범위 조정이나 확실성 판별 같은 hard 특성이 실질적으로 요구되지 않는다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Great Green Wall is an initiative launched by the African Union in 2007.
- Its original plan was to plant a continuous band of trees roughly 8,000 kilometers long across the Sahel, from Senegal to Djibouti.
- Over time, organizers shifted from a single tree line toward a mosaic of land-restoration practices, such as protecting naturally regrowing shrubs and building water-catching earthworks.
- In Niger, farmer-managed regeneration of native trees has restored vegetation on about 5 million hectares.
- The initiative is funded by a mix of national governments and international donors.

The student wants to emphasize how the Great Green Wall's approach has changed since it began. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Great Green Wall is an initiative launched by the African Union in 2007.
- Its original plan was to plant a continuous band of trees roughly 8,000 kilometers long across the Sahel, from Senegal to Djibouti.
- Over time, organizers shifted from a single tree line toward a mosaic of land-restoration practices, such as protecting naturally regrowing shrubs and building water-catching earthworks.
- In Niger, farmer-managed regeneration of native trees has restored vegetation on about 5 million hectares.
- The initiative is funded by a mix of national governments and international donors.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how the Great Green Wall's approach has changed since it began. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although the Great Green Wall was first envisioned as a continuous 8,000-kilometer band of trees across the Sahel, it has since become a mosaic of varied land-restoration practices.
In Niger, farmers who manage the regeneration of native trees have restored vegetation on about 5 million hectares.
Launched by the African Union in 2007, the Great Green Wall is a Sahel-wide effort that is supported by national governments and international donors and that includes many restoration activities.
The Great Green Wall depends on funding from both national governments and international donors, a mix that has sustained the initiative since 2007.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 '접근 방식의 변화'를 강조하는 것이다. A는 원래 계획(연속된 8,000km 나무 띠)과 이후의 방식(다양한 토지 복원 방식의 모자이크)을 대비시켜 변화를 직접 드러낸다.
B(지나치게 세부적): 니제르 한 곳의 성과만 담고 있어, 원래 계획과 비교해 무엇이 바뀌었는지 보여 주지 않는다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 시작 연도, 자금, 활동을 한데 묶어 사업 전체를 개관할 뿐, '변화'라는 초점이 사라졌다. 'many restoration activities'라는 표현도 처음 계획과 대비되지 않는다.
D(관련 없는 항목 강조): 자금 구조를 강조하는데, 이는 접근 방식의 변화와 상관이 없다. 'since 2007'이 시간의 흐름을 떠올리게 하지만 변화를 말하지는 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer: A. The goal is to emphasize how the approach has changed. Choice A sets the original plan (a continuous 8,000-kilometer band of trees) against the later approach (a mosaic of varied restoration practices), so it shows the change directly.
B is too narrow. It reports only one result in Niger and never compares the approach to the original plan.
C is too broad. It combines the launch date, the funding, and the activities into a general overview, so the focus on change is lost. Its phrase "many restoration activities" is never contrasted with how the project began.
D focuses on the wrong note. It emphasizes funding, which has nothing to do with a change in approach. "Since 2007" suggests time passing, but the choice never describes any change.

hardJudge.note: 목표 '접근 방식의 변화 강조'가 명확하며, 정답 A는 노트 2·3을 Although로 대비·통합해 변화의 방향(단일 나무 띠→복원 방식 모자이크)을 정확히 드러낸다. B는 니제르 단일 성과로 지나치게 구체적, C는 연도·자금·활동을 모두 묶은 개관으로 지나치게 포괄적, D는 자금 구조라는 무관 초점에 'since 2007'로 시간성을 가장한 매력적 오답이다. 해설은 각 오답의 결함을 정확히 지적하고 모순 없음. 사실 관계(2007 AU 출범, 약 8,000km, 세네갈~지부티, 니제르 약 500만 ha 재생)도 공지된 자료와 부합. 단순 사실 선택이 아니라 두 노트를 대비 구조로 종합해야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구하며, 난이도가 계산량·길이에서 오지 않는다.

advisory.note: 정답이 맞다. 변화를 드러내는 문장은 'Although ... first envisioned ... has since become' 구조를 가진 A뿐이다. 그러나 오답 셋 모두 '변화'를 전혀 언급하지 않아 키워드만 대조해도 바로 걸러진다. 그래서 목표 범위를 따져 보는 판단(purpose_scope_calibration)이 실제로는 필요하지 않다. 정답 A는 노트 두 항목을 합친 것이지만 그 결합이 뻔해서 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 확실성 수준 구분이나 관계 방향 판단 같은 함정도 없다. 오답 C에 'many restoration activities'가 들어 있지만 변화를 뜻하는 표현이 없어 함정으로 작동하지 못한다.

problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mariana Okafor studied whether urban street lighting affects moth pollination of evening primrose plants.
- Okafor's team installed LED streetlights at 12 previously unlit meadow sites and left 12 comparable sites dark.
- Over two summers, plants at lit sites received 41% fewer moth visits than plants at dark sites; this difference was directly counted from video recordings.
- Plants at lit sites also produced somewhat fewer seeds, but the seed difference was small and may have been influenced by variation in soil moisture between sites.
- Okafor concluded that the effect of lighting on seed production remains uncertain and requires further study.
problem.question: The student wants to present Okafor's findings while accurately conveying how firmly each result was established. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Okafor's team found that evening primrose plants at lit meadow sites received 41% fewer moth visits than those at dark sites, but whether the lighting also reduced seed production is not yet clear.
Okafor's team found that LED streetlights reduced moth visits to evening primrose plants by 41% and, as a result, caused the plants to produce fewer seeds.
Okafor's team found that evening primrose plants at lit meadow sites may have received fewer moth visits than those at dark sites, and lighting might possibly affect seed production as well.
Okafor's team found that evening primrose plants at lit meadow sites produced 41% fewer seeds than those at dark sites, though the effect of lighting on moth visits is not yet clear.
problem.explanation: 정답 A: 영상으로 직접 센 방문 수 41% 감소는 확정적으로, 토양 수분 영향 가능성이 있는 종자 생산 효과는 불확실하다고 표현해 노트의 확실성 수준과 일치한다. B: 잠정적인 종자 감소를 조명이 '야기했다'고 확정적으로 과장했다. C: 직접 계수된 방문 감소를 'may have'로 불필요하게 축소했다. D: 확정/잠정이라는 구조는 맞지만 41%를 종자 수치로, 불확실성을 방문 수로 뒤바꿔 연구 내용을 혼동했다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct: it states the 41% drop in moth visits firmly, since the team counted those visits directly from video, and it presents the effect on seeds as unclear, since that difference was small and may have come from soil moisture. B overstates a tentative result by claiming the lighting caused fewer seeds. C weakens a firm finding by saying the plants only "may have" received fewer visits. D uses the right mix of firm and tentative wording but swaps the findings: it attaches the 41% to seeds and the uncertainty to moth visits.

hardJudge.note: 노트 3(직접 계수, 확정)과 노트 4·5(잠정)가 명확히 구분되어 있고 A가 이를 정확히 반영. B는 과잉 일반화(인과 단정), C는 확실성 과도 축소, D는 수치·불확실성 뒤바꿈으로 네 선지 모두 기능적으로 구별됨. 해설 수치·논리 일치. 가상의 연구자 이름 사용으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 맞고 해설도 정확하다. 다만 오답 구조가 너무 뻔하다. B는 과잉 일반화, C는 확실성 과소 표현, D는 사실을 뒤바꾼 오답이라 쉽게 걸러진다. 노트의 '41%, directly counted'와 'remains uncertain'이 신호를 그대로 드러내서 표면적인 단서 대조만으로 풀린다. 확정/잠정 구분은 이 레시피의 기본 요구일 뿐이고, 그 이상의 사고(목적 범위 판단, 관계 방향 판별 등)는 요구하지 않는다. 그래서 전형적인 medium 문항 수준이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

The student wants to emphasize that the two telescopes benefit from dry air for different reasons. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) is a radio telescope located on the Chajnantor plateau in Chile.
- ALMA sits at an altitude of about 5,000 meters, where the dry air absorbs little of the millimeter-wavelength light it detects.
- ALMA consists of 66 antennas that work together as a single instrument.
- The South Pole Telescope (SPT) is located at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station in Antarctica.
- SPT sits at an altitude of about 2,800 meters, but the extreme cold keeps the air above it exceptionally dry.
- SPT uses a single 10-meter dish.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize that the two telescopes benefit from dry air for different reasons. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: ALMA owes its dry observing conditions to its high altitude of about 5,000 meters, whereas SPT, at only about 2,800 meters, relies instead on the extreme Antarctic cold to keep the air above it dry.
Located at an altitude of about 5,000 meters on Chile's Chajnantor plateau, ALMA benefits from dry air that absorbs little of the millimeter-wavelength light it detects.
While ALMA combines 66 antennas into a single instrument at an altitude of about 5,000 meters, SPT uses a single 10-meter dish at about 2,800 meters.
Both ALMA and SPT benefit from dry air, but because SPT is located at a lower altitude, its observations are less precise than those made by ALMA.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 두 망원경이 '서로 다른 이유'로 건조한 공기의 이점을 얻는다는 점을 강조하는 것이다. A는 ALMA는 높은 고도, SPT는 극한의 추위라는 두 원인을 대비해 결합한다.
B: ALMA에 관한 사실만 담아 SPT와의 대비가 없으므로 목표를 절반만 달성한다.
C: 두 망원경의 정보를 결합했지만 안테나 구성과 고도를 비교할 뿐, 건조한 공기의 원인 차이를 말하지 않는다.
D: '관측 정밀도가 낮다'는 내용은 노트에 없으며, 낮은 고도를 단점으로 왜곡해 SPT가 추위로 건조함을 얻는다는 사실을 누락한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The goal is to emphasize that the two telescopes get the benefit of dry air for different reasons. A contrasts those two causes in one sentence: ALMA gets dry air from its high altitude, and SPT gets it from the extreme Antarctic cold.
B: It covers only ALMA. There's no contrast with SPT, so it does only half of what the goal asks.
C: It does combine information about both telescopes, but it compares their antenna setups and altitudes. It never says why each one has dry air.
D: The claim that SPT's observations are less precise doesn't appear anywhere in the notes. It also treats lower altitude as a weakness and leaves out the fact that cold is what keeps the air above SPT dry.

hardJudge.note: 노트 6개 중 목표(건조한 공기의 '서로 다른 이유')에 맞는 두 원인(고도 vs 추위)을 골라 대비해야 하며, C처럼 두 망원경을 모두 다루지만 초점이 다른 선택지가 유혹지로 기능해 단순 사실 선택을 넘어선다. A는 노트 사실과 일치하고 B(한쪽만), C(초점 불일치), D(노트 외 내용·왜곡) 모두 명확히 배제 가능. 사실 정보(ALMA 5,000m·66안테나, SPT 2,800m·10m 단일 접시, 남극 건조 공기)도 실제와 부합.

advisory.note: C는 두 대상을 비교하지만 목표와 무관한 축(안테나 수·고도)을 다루는 그럴듯한 오답이라, '서로 다른 이유'라는 인과 축을 골라내야 한다. 다만 정답 A에 쓰인 'owes', 'relies instead' 같은 표현이 목표 문구와 거의 그대로 겹쳐서 난이도는 hard의 하한 수준이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Sea otters in California's Elkhorn Slough estuary were locally extinct for about a century before returning in the 1980s.
- In the slough, sea otters eat large numbers of shore crabs, which otherwise graze heavily on eelgrass-cleaning sea slugs.
- With fewer crabs, sea slugs thrive and remove algae that would otherwise smother eelgrass blades.
- Researcher Brent Hughes found that eelgrass beds expanded markedly after otters recolonized the slough, even though the water remained polluted by agricultural nutrients.
- Hughes's study was published in 2013 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
- Elkhorn Slough is also an important stopover for migrating shorebirds.

The student wants to emphasize how the sea otters' return benefited eelgrass despite poor water quality. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Sea otters in California's Elkhorn Slough estuary were locally extinct for about a century before returning in the 1980s.
- In the slough, sea otters eat large numbers of shore crabs, which otherwise graze heavily on eelgrass-cleaning sea slugs.
- With fewer crabs, sea slugs thrive and remove algae that would otherwise smother eelgrass blades.
- Researcher Brent Hughes found that eelgrass beds expanded markedly after otters recolonized the slough, even though the water remained polluted by agricultural nutrients.
- Hughes's study was published in 2013 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
- Elkhorn Slough is also an important stopover for migrating shorebirds.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how the sea otters' return benefited eelgrass despite poor water quality. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: By eating shore crabs, returning sea otters allowed algae-removing sea slugs to flourish, helping Elkhorn Slough's eelgrass beds expand even though nutrient pollution persisted.
In Elkhorn Slough, sea otters eat large numbers of shore crabs, which graze heavily on sea slugs that clean eelgrass.
Elkhorn Slough, an estuary where sea otters returned in the 1980s after a century of absence, supports eelgrass, sea slugs, crabs, and migrating shorebirds.
Brent Hughes's 2013 study of Elkhorn Slough, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, examined an estuary that serves as a key stopover for migrating shorebirds.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 '수달 복귀가 수질 악화에도 불구하고 잘피(eelgrass)에 이익을 주었다'는 점을 강조하는 것이다. A는 수달→게 감소→갯민숭달팽이 번성→조류 제거로 이어지는 연쇄를 압축하고, 잘피 확장과 영양염 오염 지속('despite')을 함께 제시해 목표의 두 요소를 모두 충족한다.
B(지나치게 세부적): 먹이 관계의 한 고리만 서술할 뿐 잘피가 실제로 확장되었다는 결과와 수질 악화라는 대비가 빠져 있다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 습지의 생물 목록을 나열하는 개관에 그쳐 수달이 잘피에 준 이익이라는 초점과 수질 대비를 잃었다.
D(무관한 항목 강조): 출판 정보와 철새 기착지라는 목표와 무관한 메모를 부각하며, 수달이나 잘피 이익을 전혀 언급하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer: A. Your goal is to emphasize that the otters' return helped eelgrass even though the water quality stayed poor. A covers the whole chain: otters eat crabs, so sea slugs flourish and clear away algae, and the eelgrass beds expand. It also includes the contrast with continuing nutrient pollution ("even though"), so it meets both parts of the goal.
Why the others are wrong:
B is too detailed. It describes only one link in the food chain. It never says that eelgrass actually expanded, and it leaves out the contrast with poor water quality.
C is too broad. It just lists the organisms in the slough, like a general overview. It loses the focus on how otters benefited eelgrass and says nothing about water quality.
D highlights the wrong notes. It focuses on publication details and the shorebird stopover, which don't relate to the goal. It never mentions otters helping eelgrass.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 수달→게→갯민숭달팽이→조류 제거→잘피 확장이라는 4단계 영양 연쇄(메모 2·3·4)를 한 문장으로 통합하고, 목표의 핵심 대비('despite poor water quality')를 'even though nutrient pollution persisted'로 정확히 반영한다. B는 먹이 관계의 단일 고리만(결과·수질 대비 누락, 과도 구체), C는 생물 목록 개관(과도 포괄), D는 출판 정보·철새(무관)로 분류가 명확하다. Hughes 2013 PNAS 연구, 1980년대 수달 복귀 등 사실 관계도 실제와 부합. 다만 D가 수달·잘피를 전혀 언급하지 않아 소거가 다소 쉬운 편이며, B와 A의 변별이 주요 난이도 요소다. hard 특성 중 multi_source 통합과 'despite' 관계 방향 판별을 실제로 요구하므로 hard 적합 판정.

advisory.note: 정답 A만 '이익'과 '수질 불량에도 불구하고'라는 두 요소를 모두 담고 있다. B, C, D는 'despite' 대비가 전혀 없어 키워드 대조만으로 바로 걸러진다. 그래서 여러 메모를 종합해야 하는 것처럼 보이지만 실제로는 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 오답이 정답과 겨룰 만큼 그럴듯하지 않고, 수준을 정밀하게 맞춰야 할 필요도 없다. B는 '지나치게 구체적'이라기보다 결과가 빠진 불완전한 진술에 가깝다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mira Castellanos studied mangrove forests along the coast of Belize.
- Her team confirmed through direct measurement that mangrove root mats at the study sites had trapped sediment layers up to 40 centimeters thick over two decades.
- Using a statistical model, the team estimated that these root mats may reduce storm-surge wave height by roughly 30 percent, though the estimate carries wide uncertainty.
- In a separate study, hydrologist Anil Mehta found that seagrass meadows in the same region measurably slowed shoreline erosion.
- Castellanos noted that more field data from actual storms are needed to test the wave-height estimate.

The student wants to present Castellanos's findings while accurately conveying how certain each finding is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mira Castellanos studied mangrove forests along the coast of Belize.
- Her team confirmed through direct measurement that mangrove root mats at the study sites had trapped sediment layers up to 40 centimeters thick over two decades.
- Using a statistical model, the team estimated that these root mats may reduce storm-surge wave height by roughly 30 percent, though the estimate carries wide uncertainty.
- In a separate study, hydrologist Anil Mehta found that seagrass meadows in the same region measurably slowed shoreline erosion.
- Castellanos noted that more field data from actual storms are needed to test the wave-height estimate.
problem.question: The student wants to present Castellanos's findings while accurately conveying how certain each finding is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Castellanos's team measured sediment layers up to 40 centimeters thick trapped by mangrove root mats in Belize, and their model suggests the mats might cut storm-surge wave height by about 30 percent, pending further storm data.
Castellanos's team showed that mangrove root mats in Belize trap sediment layers up to 40 centimeters thick and reduce storm-surge wave height by 30 percent.

Castellanos's team found that mangrove root mats in Belize may have trapped sediment layers up to 40 centimeters thick, and their model suggests the mats might cut storm-surge wave height by about 30 percent.
