Castellanos's team measured sediment layers up to 40 centimeters thick trapped by mangrove root mats in Belize, and their model suggests the mats might measurably slow shoreline erosion, pending further field data.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 퇴적층 40cm는 직접 측정으로 '확인된' 사실이므로 확정적으로 쓰고, 파고 30% 감소는 불확실성이 큰 통계 모델 추정이므로 'suggests', 'might', 'pending further storm data'처럼 잠정적으로 표현했다. 따라서 두 결과의 확실성 수준이 모두 노트와 맞는다.
B: 파고 30% 감소를 'showed … reduce'로 확정된 것처럼 써서 잠정적 추정을 과장했다.
C: 직접 측정으로 확인된 퇴적층 결과를 'may have trapped'로 써서 확정된 사실을 불필요하게 불확실한 것처럼 축소했다.
D: 확실성 수준은 맞지만, '해안 침식 완화'는 Mehta의 해초지 연구 결과이므로 Castellanos의 맹그로브 모델과 혼동했다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The 40-centimeter sediment layers were confirmed by direct measurement, so they should be stated as fact. The 30 percent wave-height reduction is a model estimate with wide uncertainty, so it needs hedged wording like "suggests," "might," and "pending further storm data." Choice A matches the certainty of both findings.
B: It uses "showed … reduce" for the wave-height reduction. That presents an uncertain model estimate as proven fact.
C: It says "may have trapped" about the sediment layers. That makes a directly measured, confirmed finding sound uncertain when it isn't.
D: Its level of certainty is right, but slowing shoreline erosion comes from Mehta's separate seagrass study. It wrongly attributes that finding to Castellanos's mangrove model.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 확정(직접 측정 40cm)과 잠정(모델 추정 30%, 불확실성 큼, 추가 데이터 필요)이 명확히 구분됨. A는 'measured' + 'suggests/might/pending' 으로 확실성 수준을 정확히 반영. B는 과잉 일반화(showed…reduce), C는 확정 사실을 'may have trapped'로 과소 축소, D는 Mehta의 해초지 결과(침식 완화)를 Castellanos 연구로 잘못 귀속(출처 혼동 오답). 해설은 각 선지 판정과 일치하며 모순 없음. 형식(노트 5개, 목표 진술, 4지선다) 적합. 다중 출처 구분(Mehta vs Castellanos)과 확실성 등급 판별을 동시에 요구하므로 medium 이상.

advisory.note: 두 결과의 확실성 수준을 각각 따로 맞춰야 하고, D는 다른 연구 출처(Mehta)를 섞어 넣는 함정이라 medium보다 한 단계 더 생각해야 한다. 다만 B의 'showed'와 C의 'may have'처럼 단서가 비교적 눈에 띄어서 hard 기준에서는 하한선에 가깝다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Glass frogs (family Centrolenidae) live in the rainforests of Central and South America.
- When a glass frog sleeps, it pulls about 89% of its red blood cells out of circulation and stores them in its liver.
- This makes the frog's body up to about 61% more transparent, helping it hide from predators.
- Most vertebrates cannot pool that much blood without forming dangerous clots.
- The pale belly of the Atlantic herring is a different way of avoiding detection: the fish is hard to see from below against the bright surface water.

The student wants to explain how the glass frog's sleeping behavior produces a camouflage benefit. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Glass frogs (family Centrolenidae) live in the rainforests of Central and South America.
- When a glass frog sleeps, it pulls about 89% of its red blood cells out of circulation and stores them in its liver.
- This makes the frog's body up to about 61% more transparent, helping it hide from predators.
- Most vertebrates cannot pool that much blood without forming dangerous clots.
- The pale belly of the Atlantic herring is a different way of avoiding detection: the fish is hard to see from below against the bright surface water.
problem.question: The student wants to explain how the glass frog's sleeping behavior produces a camouflage benefit. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: By storing about 89% of its red blood cells in its liver while it sleeps, the glass frog becomes up to about 61% more transparent, which helps it hide from predators.
While it sleeps, the glass frog, which lives in the rainforests of Central and South America, pulls about 89% of its red blood cells out of circulation and stores them in its liver.
The glass frog becomes up to about 61% more transparent while it sleeps, whereas the Atlantic herring relies on its pale belly to be hard to see from below.
By storing about 89% of its red blood cells in its liver while it sleeps, the glass frog becomes up to about 61% more transparent, allowing it to stay hidden from predators during both day and night.
problem.explanation: 목표는 수면 중 행동(원인)과 위장 효과(결과)를 연결하는 것이다. A는 '적혈구 89%를 간에 저장'이라는 사실과 '투명도 최대 61% 증가로 포식자 회피'라는 사실을 인과 관계로 결합하므로 정답이다. B는 행동만 서술하고 위장 효과는 빠져 있어 목표를 절반만 달성한다. C는 두 사실을 결합했지만 청어와 비교하는 데 그쳐 행동이 어떻게 위장으로 이어지는지 설명하지 않는다. D는 노트에 없는 '낮과 밤 모두'라는 내용을 덧붙였다. 노트에 따르면 이 효과는 잠잘 때에만 나타나므로 사실을 왜곡한다.
problem.explanationEn: The goal is to connect the frog's sleeping behavior (the cause) to its camouflage benefit (the effect). Choice A combines the fact that the frog stores about 89% of its red blood cells in its liver with the fact that this makes it up to 61% more transparent and helps it hide from predators. It links the two as cause and effect, so A is correct. Choice B describes only the behavior and leaves out the camouflage benefit, so it meets just half the goal. Choice C combines two facts, but it compares the frog with the herring instead of explaining how the behavior creates camouflage. Choice D adds something that isn't in the notes, "during both day and night." The notes tie the effect to sleep only, so D distorts the facts.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 행동(적혈구 간 저장)→결과(투명도 증가)→이익(포식자 회피)의 인과를 정확히 통합. B는 행동만, C는 비교 목적으로 방향이 어긋남, D는 정답과 거의 동일하나 '낮과 밤 모두'라는 노트 밖 과잉 범위를 덧붙여 미세한 범위 판별을 요구하므로 medium 이상의 사고가 필요. 과학적 수치(89%, 61%, Centrolenidae 분포)는 2022년 Science 연구와 일치.

advisory.note: A는 행동(원인)과 위장 효과(결과)를 함께 담고 있어 정답이다. 그러나 정답을 고르려면 핵심 단어 '수면 행동 → 위장 효과'를 맞추기만 하면 된다. B(사실 하나만 담음), C(비교로 목표에서 벗어남), D(노트에 없는 정보 추가)는 모두 전형적인 오답 유형이라 쉽게 걸러진다. 확실성 수준 구분, 관계의 방향 판단, 정보 범위 조정 같은 hard 특성을 실제로 요구하지 않으므로 medium 수준의 문항이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Uros people live on Lake Titicaca, which straddles the border between Peru and Bolivia.
- For centuries, the Uros have built floating islands from totora, a reed that grows in the lake's shallows.
- Each island rests on blocks of buoyant totora root mass, which are anchored to the lakebed with ropes and stakes.
- Because the submerged reeds steadily rot, residents must add fresh layers of reeds to the surface every few weeks.
- Some islands today host solar panels and welcome tourists who arrive by boat from the city of Puno.

The student wants to emphasize that maintaining the Uros islands requires ongoing effort. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Uros people live on Lake Titicaca, which straddles the border between Peru and Bolivia.
- For centuries, the Uros have built floating islands from totora, a reed that grows in the lake's shallows.
- Each island rests on blocks of buoyant totora root mass, which are anchored to the lakebed with ropes and stakes.
- Because the submerged reeds steadily rot, residents must add fresh layers of reeds to the surface every few weeks.
- Some islands today host solar panels and welcome tourists who arrive by boat from the city of Puno.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize that maintaining the Uros islands requires ongoing effort. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Uros islands rest on blocks of buoyant totora root mass that are held in place by ropes and stakes driven into the bed of Lake Titicaca.
Living on Lake Titicaca between Peru and Bolivia, the Uros have for centuries built floating islands of totora reeds, some of which now feature solar panels and draw tourists from Puno.
Since the totora reeds beneath them constantly decay, the floating islands of the Uros must be rebuilt from the top, with residents laying down fresh reeds every few weeks.
Some Uros islands now host solar panels and receive tourists who travel by boat from the nearby city of Puno.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 물속 갈대가 계속 썩어 몇 주마다 새 갈대를 덧대야 한다는 정보로 '지속적 노력'이라는 목표를 정확히 강조한다.
A(지나치게 세부적): 섬의 구조·고정 방식이라는 기술적 세부만 제시하며, 유지에 반복적 노력이 든다는 점은 드러나지 않는다. 밧줄·말뚝을 '유지 작업'으로 착각하기 쉽다.
B(지나치게 포괄적): 위치·역사·현대적 변화까지 개관하여 초점을 잃었고, 유지 노력은 전혀 언급하지 않는다.
D(무관한 항목 강조): 태양광 패널과 관광이라는 현대적 측면만 강조해 목표와 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
C is correct: it states that the submerged reeds constantly decay, so residents must add fresh reeds every few weeks, which directly emphasizes the ongoing effort maintenance requires.
A is too detailed: it describes how the islands are built and anchored, but that structural detail doesn't show any repeated work. It's easy to mistake anchoring for maintenance, but anchoring isn't ongoing upkeep.
B is too broad: it gives an overview of location, history, and modern features, losing focus, and it never mentions maintenance at all.
D emphasizes an unrelated note (solar panels and tourism), which has nothing to do with upkeep.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 갈대 부패(원인)→몇 주마다 새 갈대 추가(지속적 노력)라는 인과를 결합해 목표에 정확히 부합. A는 구조·고정 방식이라는 정적 세부를 '유지'로 오인하게 하는 유효한 지나치게 구체적 오답, B는 위치·역사·현대 변화를 개관하는 지나치게 포괄적 오답, D는 목표와 무관. 노트 사실(티티카카호 위치, 토토라, 푸노)은 정확. C의 'rebuilt from the top'은 노트의 'add fresh layers to the surface'의 수용 가능한 환언. 다만 난이도는 hard 중 하한에 가까움(정답 단서가 비교적 직접적).

advisory.note: 정답 C만 노트 4(갈대가 썩어 몇 주마다 덧대야 함)를 사용하고, 오답들은 모두 그 정보를 아예 다루지 않음. 따라서 '반복적 노력' 키워드만 맞추면 바로 풀리는 전형적 medium 문항임. 여러 노트를 종합하거나 범위를 보정할 필요가 없어 hard 특성이 없음. 'rebuilt from the top'은 'add fresh layers'를 약간 확대한 표현이나 허용 범위임.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Marisol Ortega studied Pacific chorus frogs living near highways in Oregon.
- Ortega recorded that frogs at roadside ponds called at a higher pitch than frogs at quiet ponds; this pitch difference was measured directly in every population she sampled.
- She also found that roadside populations had somewhat lower breeding success, but she cautioned that this pattern was weak and might be explained by other factors, such as road runoff.
- Separately, Ortega observed that roadside frogs began calling about 40 minutes later in the evening than frogs at quiet ponds.
- Ortega has proposed that higher-pitched calls may help frogs be heard over low-frequency traffic noise.

The student wants to present Ortega's findings about pitch and breeding success while accurately reflecting how certain each finding is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Marisol Ortega studied Pacific chorus frogs living near highways in Oregon.
- Ortega recorded that frogs at roadside ponds called at a higher pitch than frogs at quiet ponds; this pitch difference was measured directly in every population she sampled.
- She also found that roadside populations had somewhat lower breeding success, but she cautioned that this pattern was weak and might be explained by other factors, such as road runoff.
- Separately, Ortega observed that roadside frogs began calling about 40 minutes later in the evening than frogs at quiet ponds.
- Ortega has proposed that higher-pitched calls may help frogs be heard over low-frequency traffic noise.
problem.question: The student wants to present Ortega's findings about pitch and breeding success while accurately reflecting how certain each finding is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ortega found that roadside Pacific chorus frogs call at a higher pitch than frogs at quiet ponds, and that traffic noise lowers these frogs' breeding success.
Ortega's data suggest that roadside Pacific chorus frogs might call at a slightly higher pitch than frogs at quiet ponds and might also have somewhat lower breeding success.
Ortega found that roadside Pacific chorus frogs call at a higher pitch than frogs at quiet ponds; they may also breed somewhat less successfully, though this weak pattern could have other causes.

Ortega found that roadside Pacific chorus frogs start calling about 40 minutes later than frogs at quiet ponds; they may also breed somewhat less successfully, though this weak pattern could have other causes.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 음높이 차이는 모든 표본에서 직접 측정된 확정적 결과이므로 'found'로 단정하고, 번식 성공률 저하는 약하고 다른 요인(도로 유출수)으로 설명될 수 있다는 단서가 있으므로 'may'와 단서를 붙여 잠정적으로 제시했다.
A: 잠정적인 번식 성공률 결과를 교통 소음이 원인이라는 확정적 인과로 과장했다.
B: 직접 측정된 확정적 사실인 음높이 차이를 'might'로 불필요하게 축소했다.
D: 확실성 수준 표현은 맞지만, 목표가 요구한 음높이 결과 대신 별개 관찰인 울음 시작 시각 지연을 넣어 다른 연구 내용과 혼동했다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice C is correct. The pitch difference was measured directly in every population, so it should be stated with certainty ("found"). The breeding-success pattern was weak and might be explained by other factors, so it should be hedged ("may," "could have other causes"). C does both.
Choice A overstates the tentative breeding finding. It presents it as a definite causal claim that traffic noise lowers breeding success.
Choice B goes the other way: it uses "might" for the pitch difference, which was a directly measured, certain finding.
Choice D hedges the right claim at the right level, but it reports the later calling start time instead of the pitch finding the goal asks for.

hardJudge.note: C correctly states pitch as definitive ('found') and breeding success as tentative with caveat. A overreaches (causal claim via traffic noise), B under-hedges a directly measured result (and adds unsupported 'slightly'), D substitutes an irrelevant finding (timing delay). Requires distinguishing certainty levels across two findings and filtering distractor notes; appropriate for hard.

advisory.note: C는 음높이를 확정적으로, 번식 결과를 잠정적으로 정확히 표현함. A는 과잉 일반화·인과 과장, B는 확실성 과소, D는 목표와 무관한 정보 대체로 함정 구성이 적절함. 다만 목표 문장에 'certain'이 명시돼 단서가 직접적이어서 hard 난이도로서는 경계선 수준임.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Mangroves and seagrass meadows are both coastal ecosystems that store carbon, often called "blue carbon."
- Mangrove forests grow along tropical shorelines in the intertidal zone.
- Mangroves store most of their carbon in waterlogged soils beneath the trees.
- Seagrass meadows grow fully underwater in shallow coastal seas.
- Seagrass meadows store most of their carbon in sediments trapped among their roots.
- Both ecosystems are being lost to coastal development.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity in how the two ecosystems store carbon. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Mangroves and seagrass meadows are both coastal ecosystems that store carbon, often called "blue carbon."
- Mangrove forests grow along tropical shorelines in the intertidal zone.
- Mangroves store most of their carbon in waterlogged soils beneath the trees.
- Seagrass meadows grow fully underwater in shallow coastal seas.
- Seagrass meadows store most of their carbon in sediments trapped among their roots.
- Both ecosystems are being lost to coastal development.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity in how the two ecosystems store carbon. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Mangroves, which grow along tropical shorelines in the intertidal zone, store most of their carbon in waterlogged soils beneath the trees.
Although mangroves grow in the intertidal zone and seagrass meadows grow fully underwater, both ecosystems are being lost to coastal development.
Whether in the waterlogged soils beneath mangroves or the sediments among seagrass roots, both ecosystems keep most of their carbon below ground rather than in their living plants.
Mangroves and seagrass meadows both store most of their carbon in the soil or sediment beneath them, holding several times more carbon per acre than tropical rainforests do.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 맹그로브(나무 아래 물에 잠긴 토양)와 해초(뿌리 사이 퇴적물)의 탄소 저장 방식을 함께 제시하고, 둘 다 땅속에 저장한다는 공통점을 짚어 목표를 달성한다. 노트에서 대부분의 탄소가 토양·퇴적물에 있다고 했으므로 '살아 있는 식물이 아니라'는 표현도 메모 내용에서 바로 따라 나온다.
A: 맹그로브만 다루므로 비교 대상이 없어 공통점을 보여 주지 못한다(목표의 절반만 달성).
B: 두 생태계를 함께 다루지만, 결합한 사실이 서식지의 차이와 개발로 인한 소실이다. 탄소 저장의 공통점이라는 목표와 무관하다.
D: 공통점은 맞게 말하지만, '열대우림보다 에이커당 몇 배 많다'는 노트에 없는 내용을 덧붙여 사실을 왜곡한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: This choice connects two separate notes. Mangroves store carbon in the waterlogged soils beneath the trees, and seagrass stores it in the sediments among its roots. C combines these facts to point out what they share: both ecosystems store their carbon below ground. The notes say "most" of the carbon is in soil or sediment, so the phrase "rather than in their living plants" follows directly from them.
A: This choice describes only mangroves. With nothing to compare them to, it can't show a similarity, so it meets only half of the goal.
B: This choice mentions both ecosystems, but the facts it combines are where they grow and the fact that both are being lost to development. Neither fact is about carbon storage, so it misses the goal.
D: The similarity it states is correct, but the comparison with tropical rainforests doesn't appear anywhere in the notes. Adding that claim misrepresents the information.

hardJudge.note: C는 노트 3·5를 결합하고 '대부분의 탄소가 토양/퇴적물에 있다'에서 '땅속, 살아있는 식물이 아님'이라는 공통점을 추상화해야 함. B는 '공통점'이기는 하나 탄소 저장이라는 목표 초점에서 벗어난 공통점이라 범위 판별이 필요하고, D는 실제로 사실인 외부 정보(열대우림 대비 저장량)를 끌어들여 매력적인 오답으로 작동. 단일 사실 선택을 넘어서는 종합 요구가 있어 medium 이상으로 판단. 세부: 해초 퇴적물을 'below ground'로 묶은 표현은 약간 느슨하지만 허용 범위.

advisory.note: 정답은 C가 맞다. '살아 있는 식물이 아니라'는 표현은 노트의 'most ... in soils/sediments'에서 합리적으로 추론할 수 있는 범위다. 다만 구조가 전형적인 medium 수준이다. A는 한쪽 사실만 담았고, B는 목표와 다른 사실을 묶었으며, D는 노트 밖 정보를 넣은 오답이라 바로 걸러진다. 목표 범위를 조정하거나 확실성 수준을 구분하는 등 hard 수준의 추가 사고는 사실상 요구하지 않는다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 2021, ecologist Mara Lindqvist studied 40 freshwater ponds in southern Sweden.
- She confirmed by direct counts that ponds bordered by reed beds contained more dragonfly larvae than ponds without reed beds.
- Her data also showed a correlation between reed-bed ponds and lower mosquito larva densities.
- Lindqvist cautioned that the data alone could not show whether dragonfly predation caused the lower mosquito numbers.
- In a separate 2019 study, researcher Tomas Berg found that reed beds lowered pond water temperatures by shading.

The student wants to present both of Lindqvist's findings while accurately reflecting how certain each one is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 2021, ecologist Mara Lindqvist studied 40 freshwater ponds in southern Sweden.
- She confirmed by direct counts that ponds bordered by reed beds contained more dragonfly larvae than ponds without reed beds.
- Her data also showed a correlation between reed-bed ponds and lower mosquito larva densities.
- Lindqvist cautioned that the data alone could not show whether dragonfly predation caused the lower mosquito numbers.
- In a separate 2019 study, researcher Tomas Berg found that reed beds lowered pond water temperatures by shading.
problem.question: The student wants to present both of Lindqvist's findings while accurately reflecting how certain each one is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Lindqvist found that reed-bed ponds held more dragonfly larvae and that these dragonflies, by preying on mosquito larvae, reduced mosquito numbers in those ponds.
Lindqvist's study suggests that reed-bed ponds may have held more dragonfly larvae, and it also found that these ponds tended to have fewer mosquito larvae, though the cause was unclear.

Lindqvist documented more dragonfly larvae in reed-bed ponds and also found that these ponds tended to have fewer mosquito larvae, though she could not determine whether dragonfly predation was responsible.
Lindqvist documented more dragonfly larvae in reed-bed ponds and also found that these ponds tended to be cooler, though she could not determine whether shading was responsible.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 잠자리 유충 수는 직접 계수로 '확인된' 사실이므로 documented로 확정적으로 쓰고, 모기 유충 감소는 상관관계일 뿐이며 인과를 밝힐 수 없다는 단서를 붙여 두 결과의 확실성 수준을 모두 정확히 반영한다.
A: 상관관계를 '포식으로 모기를 줄였다'는 인과로 과장했다(잠정적 결과의 과장).
B: 직접 계수로 확인된 잠자리 결과를 'suggests… may have'로 불필요하게 약화했다(확정적 사실의 축소).
D: 확실성 표현 구조는 맞지만, 수온 저하·그늘 효과는 Berg의 2019년 별개 연구 내용이므로 연구를 혼동했다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice C is correct. Lindqvist confirmed the dragonfly result with direct counts, so it's right to state it firmly ("documented"). The mosquito result was only a correlation, and she said she couldn't show what caused it. C keeps that caution, so it matches how certain each finding really is.
Choice A overstates the tentative finding. It claims dragonfly predation caused the lower mosquito numbers, which Lindqvist said her data couldn't show.
Choice B understates the confirmed finding. It hedges the dragonfly counts with "suggests" and "may have," even though direct counts established them.
Choice D gets the levels of certainty right, but it mixes in another study. Cooler water and shading come from Berg's separate 2019 study, not from Lindqvist's work.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 확정적(직접 계수) 진술과 잠정적(상관관계·인과 불명) 진술이 공존하고, C만이 두 수준을 정확히 반영한다. A는 인과로 과잉 일반화, B는 확정 사실을 과도하게 약화, D는 Berg의 별개 연구를 Lindqvist에 귀속시킨 출처 혼동 오답으로 매력적이다. 해설은 정답과 오답 사유를 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음. 가상의 연구자·수치라 사실 오류 문제 없음. 단일 사실 선택을 넘어 두 결과의 확실성 수준 차별화와 출처 구분을 동시에 요구하므로 hard 적합.

advisory.note: 두 결과의 확실성을 각각 다르게 표현해야 하는 이중 보정 문항. B는 확정 사실을 약화하고 A는 상관을 인과로 과장한다. D는 출처를 혼동한 함정으로, 연구 귀속까지 판단하게 만든다. 다만 A·B의 문장 구조가 비교적 눈에 띄어 hard로서는 중상 수준이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
- Beginning in the 1960s, Soviet planners diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers to irrigate cotton fields.
- Deprived of inflow, the lake shrank to roughly a tenth of its former area by the 2010s.
- In 2005, Kazakhstan completed the Kok-Aral Dam, which separated the northern part of the lake (the North Aral) from the southern part.
- Within a few years, water levels in the North Aral rose by several meters, and native fish species such as pike-perch returned.
- The southern part of the lake, cut off by the dam, continued to dry out.

The student wants to emphasize that a targeted intervention reversed part of the Aral Sea's decline. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
- Beginning in the 1960s, Soviet planners diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers to irrigate cotton fields.
- Deprived of inflow, the lake shrank to roughly a tenth of its former area by the 2010s.
- In 2005, Kazakhstan completed the Kok-Aral Dam, which separated the northern part of the lake (the North Aral) from the southern part.
- Within a few years, water levels in the North Aral rose by several meters, and native fish species such as pike-perch returned.
- The southern part of the lake, cut off by the dam, continued to dry out.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize that a targeted intervention reversed part of the Aral Sea's decline. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: After Kazakhstan's Kok-Aral Dam sealed off the North Aral in 2005, that portion of the shrinking lake rose by several meters within a few years, and native fish such as pike-perch returned.
Native pike-perch, a fish species found in the North Aral, returned to the lake's waters within a few years of 2005.

Once the world's fourth-largest lake, the Aral Sea shrank dramatically after rivers were diverted for cotton in the 1960s, and a dam built in 2005 has since affected its northern and southern parts differently.
Because Soviet planners diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers to irrigate cotton beginning in the 1960s, the Aral Sea shrank to roughly a tenth of its former area by the 2010s.
problem.explanation: 목표는 '특정한(targeted) 개입이 쇠퇴의 일부를 되돌렸다'는 점의 강조이므로 개입(Kok-Aral 댐)과 회복 결과(수위 상승, 어류 복귀)를 함께 연결해야 한다. A가 둘을 인과적으로 결합해 정답이다. B는 어류 복귀라는 세부만 담고 무엇이 회복을 가져왔는지(댐)가 빠져 지나치게 세부적이다. C는 호수의 역사 전체를 개관하며 댐의 효과를 '다르게 영향을 줬다'로 흐려 회복이라는 초점을 잃은 지나치게 포괄적인 문장이다. D는 쇠퇴의 원인과 규모만 강조해 회복이라는 목표와 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn: The goal is to emphasize that a targeted intervention reversed part of the decline, so the sentence has to connect the intervention (the Kok-Aral Dam) with what it achieved (the water rising and the fish coming back). Choice A links the two as cause and effect, so it is correct. Choice B is too detailed: it mentions only the fish returning and leaves out the dam that caused the recovery. Choice C is too broad: it summarizes the lake's whole history and says only that the dam affected the two parts "differently," which blurs the point about recovery. Choice D focuses on the causes and size of the decline, which doesn't address the recovery at all.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 개입(2005년 Kok-Aral 댐)과 회복 결과(수위 상승·어류 복귀)를 인과적으로 결합하고 '쇠퇴하던 호수'라는 맥락도 담아 '부분적 역전'이라는 목표에 정확히 부합한다. B는 댐이 빠진 지나치게 세부적인 선택지, C는 댐을 언급하지만 '다르게 영향'으로 회복 방향을 흐린 포괄적 개관, D는 쇠퇴 원인만 다뤄 목표와 무관하다. 특히 C가 개입 정보를 포함하고 있어 단순 키워드 매칭으로는 풀리지 않고, 회복이라는 방향성 판별과 범위 조정이 필요하므로 hard 특성을 충족한다. 노트·사실 관계(Kok-Aral 댐 2005년 완공, 북아랄 수위 회복, 어류 복귀)도 실제와 부합한다.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 개입(댐), 범위(북부만), 회복(수위·어류)을 함께 묶는다. C는 포괄적이지만 그럴듯한 오답이어서 범위를 따져 보게 만든다. B는 너무 세부적이고 D는 주제에서 벗어난다. 다만 B와 D는 비교적 쉽게 걸러진다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 2021, ecologist Mirela Kovač studied Eurasian otters living along two rivers in Slovenia.
- Kovač confirmed by DNA analysis of droppings that otters on the Krka River eat invasive signal crayfish.
- Crayfish remains appeared in 64% of Krka otter droppings collected in summer.
- Kovač's data suggest, but do not establish, that otter predation may slow the spread of signal crayfish upstream.
- On the Sava River, Kovač found that otters ate mainly native fish, and crayfish remains appeared in only 9% of droppings.

The student wants to present Kovač's Krka River findings while accurately distinguishing what was confirmed from what remains uncertain. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 2021, ecologist Mirela Kovač studied Eurasian otters living along two rivers in Slovenia.
- Kovač confirmed by DNA analysis of droppings that otters on the Krka River eat invasive signal crayfish.
- Crayfish remains appeared in 64% of Krka otter droppings collected in summer.
- Kovač's data suggest, but do not establish, that otter predation may slow the spread of signal crayfish upstream.
- On the Sava River, Kovač found that otters ate mainly native fish, and crayfish remains appeared in only 9% of droppings.
problem.question: The student wants to present Kovač's Krka River findings while accurately distinguishing what was confirmed from what remains uncertain. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Kovač confirmed that Krka River otters eat invasive signal crayfish, a finding that could mean the otters help slow the crayfish's spread upstream, though her data do not establish this.
Kovač confirmed that Krka River otters eat invasive signal crayfish, and because crayfish appeared in 64% of summer droppings, she showed that otter predation slows the crayfish's spread upstream.
Kovač's results suggest that Krka River otters might eat invasive signal crayfish, which could possibly help slow the crayfish's spread upstream.
Kovač confirmed that Krka River otters eat mainly native fish, a finding that could mean the otters help slow the spread of signal crayfish upstream, though her data do not establish this.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: DNA로 확인된 사실(크르카강 수달이 신호가재를 먹음)은 확정적으로, 확산 억제 효과는 노트대로 '시사하지만 입증하지 않음'으로 잠정적으로 서술해 확실성 수준을 정확히 구분한다.
B: 64%라는 수치를 근거로 확산 억제를 '보여주었다'고 써서 잠정적 결과를 확정 사실로 과장했다.
C: DNA로 확인된 먹이 관계까지 'might'로 낮춰 확정적 사실을 불필요하게 잠정적으로 축소했다.
D: 확실성 구분 구조는 A와 같지만, '주로 토종 어류를 먹는다'는 사바강 결과를 크르카강 결과와 혼동했다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice A is correct. DNA analysis confirmed that Krka River otters eat signal crayfish, so A states that as fact. The notes say the possible slowing of the crayfish's spread is only suggested, not established, and A keeps that hedge.
Choice B is wrong because it overstates the evidence. It uses the 64% figure to claim Kovač "showed" that otters slow the spread, but the notes say the data don't establish this.
Choice C is wrong because it understates the evidence. It hedges ("might eat") a diet finding that DNA analysis actually confirmed.
Choice D is wrong because it mixes up the two rivers. It uses the right levels of certainty, but eating mainly native fish was the Sava River finding, not the Krka River finding.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 DNA로 확인된 확정 사실(크르카강 수달의 신호가재 섭식)과 잠정적 추정(확산 억제 가능성, '시사하지만 입증 못함')이 함께 제시되고, A는 두 층위를 정확히 반영한다. B는 64% 수치를 근거로 확산 억제를 '보여주었다'고 과잉 일반화, C는 확정 사실을 'might'로 축소, D는 사바강 결과(주로 토종 어류)를 크르카강에 잘못 귀속해 각각 명확히 오답이다. 해설은 정답·오답 근거를 모순 없이 뒷받침한다. 확실성 수준 구분과 두 강의 정보 분리라는 추가 사고를 요구하므로 medium을 넘는다. 다만 A의 'though her data do not establish this'가 노트 문구를 거의 그대로 옮겨 단서가 다소 직접적인 점은 난이도를 약간 낮추는 요인이다. 가공 연구자 사용과 신호가재의 슬로베니아 침입종 지위는 사실적 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 확정 진술(DNA 확인)과 잠정 진술(확산 억제 시사)을 구분하는 문항으로, 과잉 일반화(B), 확실성 과소화(C), 강 혼동(D) 오답이 고르게 설계됨. D는 강을 혼동한 사실 오류라 확실성 판단 없이도 걸러지고, B·C도 노트 문구와 대조하면 비교적 쉽게 제거돼 hard로서는 경계선 수준임.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Mongolian gerbil and the fat sand rat both live in arid regions of Asia and North Africa.
- The Mongolian gerbil gets most of its water from the seeds it eats and rarely drinks free water.
- The fat sand rat eats almost exclusively the salty leaves of saltbush plants.
- To process this diet, the fat sand rat's kidneys produce urine roughly four times as concentrated as human urine.
- Both rodents are often studied by researchers interested in diabetes, because some individuals develop the disease when fed standard laboratory food.

The student wants to contrast how the two rodents cope with the challenges of a desert diet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Mongolian gerbil and the fat sand rat both live in arid regions of Asia and North Africa.
- The Mongolian gerbil gets most of its water from the seeds it eats and rarely drinks free water.
- The fat sand rat eats almost exclusively the salty leaves of saltbush plants.
- To process this diet, the fat sand rat's kidneys produce urine roughly four times as concentrated as human urine.
- Both rodents are often studied by researchers interested in diabetes, because some individuals develop the disease when fed standard laboratory food.
problem.question: The student wants to contrast how the two rodents cope with the challenges of a desert diet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the Mongolian gerbil meets its water needs largely through the seeds it eats, the fat sand rat copes with a diet of salty saltbush leaves by producing highly concentrated urine.
The fat sand rat, which feeds almost exclusively on salty saltbush leaves, has kidneys that produce urine roughly four times as concentrated as human urine.

Although the Mongolian gerbil and the fat sand rat both inhabit arid regions of Asia and North Africa, both are studied by diabetes researchers because some individuals develop the disease on laboratory food.
While the Mongolian gerbil gets its water from seeds and never needs to drink, the fat sand rat avoids water loss entirely by eating saltbush leaves, which supply all the fresh water it requires.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 게르빌은 씨앗에서 수분을 얻고, 모래쥐는 짠 잎을 진한 소변으로 처리한다는 두 사실을 대조 구조(Whereas)로 결합해 사막 식단 대처 방식의 차이를 보여 준다.
B: 모래쥐에 관한 사실만 담고 게르빌이 빠져 대조가 절반만 이루어진다.
C: 두 동물을 결합했지만 서식지·당뇨 연구라는 공통점이라 '식단 대처 방식의 대조'와 무관하다.
D: '절대 마시지 않는다(never)', '잎이 필요한 모든 담수를 공급한다'는 노트에 없는 내용이다. 노트에는 '거의 마시지 않는다(rarely)'고 되어 있고, 짠 잎을 처리하려고 신장이 진한 소변을 만든다는 사실은 왜곡되어 빠져 있다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct: it joins two separate facts, that the gerbil gets its water from seeds and that the sand rat handles salty leaves by producing concentrated urine, with a contrast word ("Whereas"). This shows how differently the two animals cope with a desert diet.
B is wrong because it talks only about the fat sand rat and leaves out the gerbil, so it never makes a contrast.
C is wrong because it does combine the two rodents, but it lists things they share (where they live and their use in diabetes research). That isn't a contrast of how they deal with their diets.
D is wrong because it adds claims the notes don't support. The notes say the gerbil "rarely" drinks, not that it never needs to. They also never say saltbush leaves supply all the sand rat's fresh water. D also drops the kidney fact that actually explains how the sand rat copes.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 두 동물의 식단 대처(씨앗 수분 vs 농축 소변)를 'Whereas'로 정확히 대조하며 노트 표현(most→largely)을 과장 없이 반영. B는 한쪽만, C는 두 동물을 묶었으나 공통점(서식지·당뇨 연구)이라 '대조' 목표와 어긋남, D는 rarely→never, '담수 전부 공급' 등 노트에 없는/왜곡된 내용. 특히 C(목표 범위 판별)와 D(확실성 과장 탐지)가 매력적 오답으로 기능해 medium 이상의 사고를 요구. 사실 측면: 노트 1의 '아시아·북아프리카'는 두 종의 분포를 합쳐 서술한 것으로 허용 가능, 소변 농축 '약 4배'도 대략적 수치로 무리 없음.

advisory.note: 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 대조형 정답(Whereas)이 표면 구조만으로 바로 식별된다. B는 한쪽 대상만 다루고, C는 주제에서 벗어나며, D는 never/entirely 같은 절대어로 쉽게 배제된다. 확실성 구분이나 범위 조정 같은 추가 사고가 실질적으로 필요하지 않다. D의 과장 표현이 너무 눈에 띄어 함정 역할을 하지 못한다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Kintsugi is a Japanese method of repairing broken ceramics.
- Repairers join the broken pieces with urushi, a lacquer made from tree sap.
- The seams are then dusted or mixed with powdered gold, so the cracks stay visible.
- Rather than hiding the damage, kintsugi treats the repair as part of the object's history.
- The practice is often traced to the late 15th century, during the time of shogun Ashikaga Yoshimasa.
- Some collectors have been reported to break pottery on purpose so it could be repaired this way.

The student wants to emphasize what makes kintsugi's approach to repair distinctive. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Kintsugi is a Japanese method of repairing broken ceramics.
- Repairers join the broken pieces with urushi, a lacquer made from tree sap.
- The seams are then dusted or mixed with powdered gold, so the cracks stay visible.
- Rather than hiding the damage, kintsugi treats the repair as part of the object's history.
- The practice is often traced to the late 15th century, during the time of shogun Ashikaga Yoshimasa.
- Some collectors have been reported to break pottery on purpose so it could be repaired this way.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize what makes kintsugi's approach to repair distinctive. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Unlike repairs meant to hide damage, kintsugi uses gold to make the cracks in broken ceramics visible, treating the repair as part of the object's history.
In kintsugi, repairers join broken ceramic pieces with urushi, a lacquer made from tree sap, and then add powdered gold to the seams.

Kintsugi, a Japanese method of repairing ceramics often traced to the late 15th century, uses lacquer and gold and has drawn so much interest that some collectors have reportedly broken pottery on purpose.
Kintsugi became so valued that some collectors were reported to break pottery on purpose just so it could be repaired with the technique.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 kintsugi의 수리 방식이 무엇 때문에 특별한지를 '강조'하는 것이다. A는 일반적인 수리(손상을 숨김)와 대비해 금으로 균열을 드러내고 수리를 사물의 역사로 여긴다는 핵심을 짚는다.
B(지나치게 세부적): 재료와 공정 단계만 나열할 뿐, 그 방식이 왜 특별한지(손상을 숨기지 않음)는 밝히지 않는다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 기원 시기, 재료, 수집가 일화까지 모두 담은 개관이라 '특별한 점'이라는 초점을 잃는다.
D(무관한 항목 강조): 수집가 일화를 강조해 수리 방식 자체가 아니라 이 기법의 인기를 부각한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer: A. The goal is to emphasize what makes kintsugi's approach to repair distinctive. A contrasts it with ordinary repairs that hide damage: kintsugi uses gold to keep the cracks visible and treats the repair as part of the object's history. That is exactly the distinctive point.
B is too detailed. It lists the materials and steps but never says why the approach stands out, which is that it doesn't hide the damage.
C is too broad. It reads like an overview that packs in the origin date, the materials, and the collector anecdote, so the focus on what's distinctive gets lost.
D emphasizes the wrong note. It highlights the collector anecdote, which shows how popular the technique is rather than what is distinctive about the repair method.

hardJudge.note: 목표(수리 방식의 '특별함' 강조)가 명확하고, 정답 A는 노트 3·4를 '손상을 숨기는 일반 수리'와의 대비 구조로 종합해 목적 범위에 정확히 맞는다. B는 재료·공정만 나열한 과잉 구체, C는 기원·재료·일화를 망라한 과잉 포괄 개관, D는 수리 방식이 아닌 인기를 부각하는 초점 이탈 오답으로 각각 기능한다. 특히 D가 '눈에 띄는 사실'이라는 점에서 그럴듯한 유인가 역할을 해, 수험생이 '수리 방식 자체의 특이성'과 '기법의 인기'를 구분해야 하므로 medium을 넘는 범위 판별이 요구된다. 사실 관계(우루시 옻칠, 금분, 아시카가 요시마사 15세기 후반 기원설)도 정확하며 해설과 정답이 일치한다.

advisory.note: 정답은 타당하다. 다만 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 정답에만 'Unlike ... hide damage' 대비 구조와 'distinctive'를 직접 가리키는 표현이 있어서 키워드 대응만으로 바로 고를 수 있다. 오답 B·C·D도 쉽게 소거된다. 확실성 구분, 관계 방향 판단 같은 추가 사고를 요구하지 않는다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Marine biologist Teresa Okafor studied cleaner wrasse, small fish that remove parasites from larger "client" fish on coral reefs.
- In aquarium trials, Okafor confirmed that wrasse removed more parasites when a client fish was watching than when no other fish was present.
- Okafor's field surveys found that reefs with more wrasse tended to have more client species visiting, but the surveys could not show whether wrasse caused the extra visits.
- She also observed that juvenile wrasse bit client fish' protective mucus more often than adults did.
- Okafor noted that further experiments are needed to determine the reason for the reef pattern.

The student wants to present both an established finding and a tentative one from Okafor's research, keeping each at the appropriate level of certainty. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Marine biologist Teresa Okafor studied cleaner wrasse, small fish that remove parasites from larger "client" fish on coral reefs.
- In aquarium trials, Okafor confirmed that wrasse removed more parasites when a client fish was watching than when no other fish was present.
- Okafor's field surveys found that reefs with more wrasse tended to have more client species visiting, but the surveys could not show whether wrasse caused the extra visits.
- She also observed that juvenile wrasse bit client fish' protective mucus more often than adults did.
- Okafor noted that further experiments are needed to determine the reason for the reef pattern.
problem.question: The student wants to present both an established finding and a tentative one from Okafor's research, keeping each at the appropriate level of certainty. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Okafor showed that cleaner wrasse remove more parasites when another fish is watching, and her surveys suggest—though they do not prove—that wrasse may attract more client species to a reef.
Okafor showed that cleaner wrasse remove more parasites when another fish is watching, and her surveys proved that wrasse draw more client species to the reefs where they live.
Okafor's work hints that cleaner wrasse might remove more parasites when another fish is watching, and her surveys suggest that wrasse may attract more client species to a reef.
Okafor showed that cleaner wrasse remove more parasites when another fish is watching, and her observations suggest that juvenile wrasse may be less able than adults to resist biting clients' mucus.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 수조 실험으로 확인된(confirmed) 결과는 확정적으로, 인과관계를 보여 주지 못한 현장 조사 결과는 'suggest… may'로 잠정적으로 표현해 두 확실성 수준을 모두 정확히 지켰다.
B: 상관관계일 뿐인 현장 조사 결과를 'proved… draw'로 단정해 잠정적 결과를 과장했다.
C: 실험으로 확인된 사실을 'hints… might'로 불필요하게 약화시켜 확정적 결과를 축소했다.
D: 'suggest… may'라는 잠정적 표현은 그럴듯하지만, 어린 개체의 점액 물기는 관찰된 사실일 뿐 '저항 능력'이라는 해석은 노트에 없으며, 노트가 잠정적이라고 밝힌 것은 산호초 패턴이다. 즉 다른 연구 내용과 혼동했다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. The aquarium result was confirmed, so stating it as fact ("showed") fits. The reef pattern is only a correlation that the surveys couldn't explain as cause and effect, so "suggest—though they do not prove—... may" is the right level of certainty for it.
B is wrong because it says the surveys "proved" that wrasse draw clients. That overstates a correlation.
C is wrong because it waters down the confirmed aquarium finding to "hints... might," which makes an established result sound uncertain.
D is wrong because, although it hedges, it hedges the wrong thing. The notes record the juvenile biting as an observation, not as the tentative finding, and the idea that juveniles are less able to resist biting doesn't appear anywhere in the notes. The tentative finding in the notes is the reef pattern.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 'confirmed' 실험 결과를 'showed'로, 인과를 입증하지 못한 현장 조사를 'suggest—though they do not prove—may'로 표현해 목표에 정확히 부합. B는 과잉 일반화(proved/draw), C는 확정 결과 축소(hints/might), D는 노트에 없는 해석('less able to resist')을 끌어오고 노트가 잠정적이라 명시한 산호초 패턴 대신 단순 관찰 사실을 잠정 진술로 바꿔 오답으로 성립. 네 번째 노트의 "client fish' protective mucus"는 "client fish's"의 오타로 보이나 정답 판정에는 영향 없음. 가공 연구자(Teresa Okafor)로 저작권·사실 오류 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 맞다. 다만 이 문항은 전형적인 medium 수준이다. B와 C는 'proved'와 'hints'라는 어휘만 보고도 쉽게 제외되고, 확정적 진술과 잠정적 진술이 노트에서 'confirmed', 'could not show', 'further experiments are needed'로 직접 표시되어 있다. D도 노트에 없는 해석이라 쉽게 걸러진다. 여러 정보를 종합하거나 목적에 맞게 범위를 판단하는 등 hard 수준의 추가 사고는 거의 요구되지 않는다.

problem.passage:
For decades, ornithologists assumed that the songs of male village weavers, a West African bird, served mainly to attract females, since males sing most intensely while building nests. Researcher Amara Diallo noticed, however, that males often continued singing long after females had chosen nests and begun laying eggs. __When Diallo played recorded weaver songs near unoccupied nests, neighboring males approached the speakers and sang back aggressively, while females largely ignored the recordings.__ Diallo therefore proposed that, at least once breeding is under way, the songs function less as courtship displays than as signals that warn rival males away from a defended territory.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: For decades, ornithologists assumed that the songs of male village weavers, a West African bird, served mainly to attract females, since males sing most intensely while building nests. Researcher Amara Diallo noticed, however, that males often continued singing long after females had chosen nests and begun laying eggs. __When Diallo played recorded weaver songs near unoccupied nests, neighboring males approached the speakers and sang back aggressively, while females largely ignored the recordings.__ Diallo therefore proposed that, at least once breeding is under way, the songs function less as courtship displays than as signals that warn rival males away from a defended territory.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents experimental results that build on an earlier observation and support the conclusion that weaver song serves a purpose other than the one long assumed.
It describes an observation that first led Diallo to doubt the traditional explanation of why male weavers sing.
It offers evidence that male weavers sing in order to attract females to their nests.
It states the main claim of the text, that weaver songs are territorial rather than courtship signals.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 앞 문장에서 Diallo는 암컷이 둥지를 고른 뒤에도 수컷이 계속 노래한다는 점을 관찰했다(의문 제기). 밑줄 문장은 이 관찰을 확인하려는 재생 실험의 결과로, 수컷은 반응하고 암컷은 무시했다는 내용이다. 이 결과가 마지막 문장의 결론, 즉 노래가 경쟁 수컷을 쫓는 영역 신호라는 주장의 근거가 된다. 앞뒤 두 단계를 모두 연결한 설명은 A뿐이다.
B 오답: 처음 의문을 품게 만든 관찰은 바로 앞 문장(번식 후에도 노래가 계속됨)이다. 밑줄 문장은 그 뒤에 이어지는 실험이므로, 인접 문장의 역할과 혼동한 선택지다.
C 오답: 암컷이 녹음을 거의 무시했으므로 실험 결과는 구애 가설을 지지하지 않고 오히려 약화한다. 지문 첫 문장의 기존 가정에만 주목한 선택지다.
D 오답: 영역 신호라는 주장은 마지막 문장에 나오는 지문 전체의 결론이다. 밑줄 문장은 그 결론을 직접 말하지 않고 근거를 제시할 뿐이다. 전체 목적과 개별 문장의 기능을 뒤바꾼 선택지다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, A: In the sentence before the underlined one, Diallo notices something puzzling: males keep singing even after females have chosen nests. The underlined sentence reports an experiment that follows up on that observation. When recorded songs were played, males responded aggressively while females ignored them. That result supports the final sentence's conclusion that the songs mainly warn off rival males. Only A connects the underlined sentence to both the observation before it and the conclusion after it.
B is wrong because the observation that first made Diallo doubt the old explanation is in the previous sentence: the continued singing after egg-laying. The underlined sentence describes the experiment that came after. B mixes up the underlined sentence with the one right before it.
C is wrong because females largely ignored the recordings, so the results actually weaken the courtship explanation. C focuses only on the assumption stated in the first sentence.
D is wrong because the claim that the songs are territorial signals is the text's overall conclusion, and it appears in the final sentence. The underlined sentence gives evidence for that claim but doesn't state it. D confuses the purpose of the whole text with the job of one sentence.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 기존 가정 → Diallo의 의문 관찰 → 재생 실험(밑줄) → 영역 신호 결론의 4단계 구조. 정답 A는 밑줄 문장이 앞 관찰을 잇고 뒤 결론을 뒷받침하는 실험 결과임을 정확히 기술하며, 이는 앞뒤 단계를 모두 연결해야 확정된다. B는 직전 문장(최초 의문 관찰)의 역할, D는 마지막 문장(전체 결론)의 역할로 인접 단계·전체 목적 혼동형 오답으로 설계됨. C는 암컷이 녹음을 무시했다는 결과와 정면 배치. 해설은 각 선택지 판정을 지문 근거로 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 가상의 연구자/실험이지만 village weaver가 서아프리카 조류라는 배경은 사실과 부합. 문장 길이는 적정하고 난이도는 단계 연결에서 비롯됨. 다만 A가 유일하게 '근거' 역할을 기술하는 선택지라 단계 역할만 파악하면 비교적 빨리 좁혀지는 점은 상위 hard 대비 다소 평이할 수 있음.

advisory.note: 지문은 기존 가정 → 반례 관찰 → 실험 → 결론의 4단계로 짜여 있다. A는 실험의 앞 단계(관찰)와 뒤 단계(결론)를 모두 연결해야 정답으로 확정된다. 오답도 각각 역할이 분명하다. B는 바로 앞 단계의 역할, C는 근거 방향을 뒤집은 것, D는 개별 문장 기능과 전체 결론을 혼동한 것이다. 지문 길이도 적절하다.

problem.passage:
Geoarchaeologist Lena Ortiz argues that a large flood around 1200 CE drove residents to abandon a once-thriving settlement along the Mississippi River. Her main evidence is a thick layer of river silt covering much of the site, which she interprets as the event that made the area uninhabitable. Historian Daniel Okafor, by contrast, studies the settlement's houses rather than its soils, counting how many house floors show signs of active use in each period. __Okafor's counts show that the number of occupied house floors had already dropped by nearly half in the decades before the silt layer was deposited.__ He links the settlement's decline to a slow breakdown in political ties among neighboring communities, a process he believes unfolded over several generations.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Geoarchaeologist Lena Ortiz argues that a large flood around 1200 CE drove residents to abandon a once-thriving settlement along the Mississippi River. Her main evidence is a thick layer of river silt covering much of the site, which she interprets as the event that made the area uninhabitable. Historian Daniel Okafor, by contrast, studies the settlement's houses rather than its soils, counting how many house floors show signs of active use in each period. __Okafor's counts show that the number of occupied house floors had already dropped by nearly half in the decades before the silt layer was deposited.__ He links the settlement's decline to a slow breakdown in political ties among neighboring communities, a process he believes unfolded over several generations.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence suggesting that the abandonment began before the event Ortiz identifies as its cause, implicitly challenging her explanation.
It offers support for Ortiz's claim by showing that the settlement's population fell sharply once the silt layer covered the site.
It describes the type of data Okafor collects, explaining why studying house floors is more reliable than studying soils.
It suggests that Okafor accepts the flood as the decisive cause of abandonment but believes political conflict made its effects worse.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Ortiz는 실트층(홍수)이 주민 이탈의 원인이라고 본다. 밑줄 문장은 실트층이 쌓이기 '이전'에 이미 거주 가옥이 절반 가까이 줄었다는 Okafor의 자료를 제시한다. 원인이 결과보다 나중에 올 수 없으므로, 이 문장은 Ortiz를 직접 언급하지 않고도 그녀의 설명을 반박하는 근거로 기능한다. 두 입장의 시간 관계를 비교해야 추론된다.
B(입장 뒤바꿈): 감소가 실트층 '이후'에 일어났다고 시간 순서를 뒤집어 Okafor의 자료를 Ortiz 지지로 잘못 서술했다.
C(한쪽 입장만 사용): Okafor의 연구 방법만 보고 판단한 것으로, 문장이 Ortiz 주장에 대해 갖는 함의를 놓쳤다. 또한 어느 방법이 더 신뢰할 만하다는 평가는 지문에 없다.
D(새로운 반응 지어냄): Okafor가 홍수를 결정적 원인으로 인정하며 절충한다는 내용은 지문에 없으며, 그는 정치적 관계 붕괴를 원인으로 본다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: Ortiz claims the flood, marked by the silt layer, caused people to abandon the settlement. The underlined sentence reports Okafor's finding that occupied house floors had already dropped by nearly half BEFORE the silt was deposited. A cause can't come after the effect it's supposed to explain, so this evidence quietly undercuts Ortiz's explanation, even though the text never says Okafor is responding to her. You can only see this by comparing the timing in the two positions.
B reverses the timeline. It claims the decline followed the silt layer, which turns Okafor's evidence into support for Ortiz.
C looks only at Okafor's method and misses what his finding means for Ortiz's claim. The text also never says that one method is more reliable than the other.
D makes up a compromise that isn't in the text. Okafor never accepts the flood as the decisive cause. He blames a slow breakdown in political ties.

hardJudge.note: Ortiz(홍수 원인)와 Okafor(정치적 붕괴, 점진적 쇠퇴) 두 입장이 명확히 구분됨. 밑줄 문장은 실트층 퇴적 '이전'에 거주 가옥이 절반 가까이 감소했다는 자료로, 명시적 반박 없이 Ortiz의 인과 설명을 시간 순서상 무력화함 — A가 정확. B는 시간 순서를 뒤집어 입장을 바꾼 오답, C는 Okafor 방법론만 보고 신뢰성 비교를 지어낸 오답, D는 지문에 없는 절충 입장을 창작한 오답으로 레시피 요건 충족. 두 입장의 시간 관계 비교와 암묵적 함의 추론이 필요하므로 medium 수준을 넘는 hard 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 옳음. 실트층보다 감소가 먼저 일어났다는 시간 순서를 근거로 Ortiz의 인과 주장을 암묵적으로 반박한다는 점을 추론해야 함. B는 시간 순서를 뒤집은 오답, C는 Okafor 쪽만 본 데다 지문에 없는 신뢰성 비교를 덧붙인 오답, D는 지어낸 절충 입장. 매력적인 오답의 강도는 다소 약하지만 hard 수준으로 인정 가능.

problem.passage:
Urban planners have long assumed that adding street trees to a neighborhood lowers summer air temperatures across the whole area. To test this, environmental engineer Lucía Ferrante placed temperature sensors along twelve residential blocks in Phoenix, Arizona, half of which had been planted with mature shade trees a decade earlier. __Ferrante found that on blocks with trees, sidewalk-level air was on average 2.1°C cooler at midafternoon than on treeless blocks, but that this difference shrank to almost nothing at night and was undetectable at sensors placed more than one block away from the plantings.__ Ferrante argues that street trees are therefore best understood as a tool for making specific walking routes more bearable during the hottest hours, rather than as a means of cooling an entire district.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Urban planners have long assumed that adding street trees to a neighborhood lowers summer air temperatures across the whole area. To test this, environmental engineer Lucía Ferrante placed temperature sensors along twelve residential blocks in Phoenix, Arizona, half of which had been planted with mature shade trees a decade earlier. __Ferrante found that on blocks with trees, sidewalk-level air was on average 2.1°C cooler at midafternoon than on treeless blocks, but that this difference shrank to almost nothing at night and was undetectable at sensors placed more than one block away from the plantings.__ Ferrante argues that street trees are therefore best understood as a tool for making specific walking routes more bearable during the hottest hours, rather than as a means of cooling an entire district.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that supports a cooling effect of trees only within limits of time and distance, which grounds the narrower role Ferrante assigns to street trees.
It presents a finding establishing that street trees lower air temperatures throughout a neighborhood, confirming the planners' long-standing assumption.
It presents a finding that trees cool sidewalks in the afternoon, which shows that trees are an effective way to make walking routes cooler at any hour.
It presents a finding suggesting that blocks with cooler sidewalks were more likely to have been chosen for tree planting, which explains why planners favored those blocks.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 오후 2.1°C 냉각 효과(지지)와 함께 야간 소멸·한 블록 밖 미검출(한계)을 제시한다. 즉 효과를 시간·공간적으로 제한된 범위에서만 입증하며, 이것이 '특정 보행로를 가장 더운 시간에 견딜 만하게 하는 도구'라는 좁은 결론과 정확히 일치한다.
B(과장): 근거는 오히려 지역 전체 냉각을 뒷받침하지 않으며, 계획가들의 가정을 확인하는 것이 아니라 제한한다.
C(부분 반영): 오후 냉각만 반영하고 야간에 효과가 사라진다는 부분을 무시해 '어느 시간대든'으로 잘못 해석했다.
D(인과 역전): 지문은 나무가 시원함을 만든다는 방향의 근거이지, 시원한 블록이 나무 식재지로 선택되었다는 내용이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, A: The underlined sentence gives evidence that supports a cooling effect (blocks with trees were 2.1°C cooler in the afternoon). It also gives the limits of that effect: the difference nearly disappeared at night, and sensors more than one block away picked up nothing. So the evidence supports cooling only at certain times and over short distances. That matches Ferrante's conclusion exactly: trees make particular walking routes more bearable during the hottest hours.
B overstates the evidence. The finding doesn't confirm cooling across a whole neighborhood. It actually narrows the planners' assumption instead of confirming it.
C uses only part of the evidence. It keeps the afternoon cooling but ignores that the effect fades at night, so "at any hour" isn't supported.
D reverses cause and effect. The text treats trees as the cause of cooler air. It never says that cooler blocks were chosen for planting.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 지지 근거(오후 2.1°C)와 한계(야간 소멸, 공간적 미검출)를 동시에 담고 있어, 수험자가 '가정 → 실험 → 제한된 결과 → 좁혀진 결론'의 논리 사슬을 재구성해야 정답 A를 고를 수 있다. B는 범위 과장, C는 야간 결과를 무시한 부분 반영(어느 시간대든), D는 나무→냉각 인과를 뒤집은 선택지로 레시피 오답 유형을 모두 충족한다. 지문의 Phoenix 실험은 가상의 연구자 설정으로 저작권·사실 오류 소지 없음. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 맞지만 오답이 너무 쉽게 걸러진다. B는 밑줄 문장 내용과 정면으로 어긋나고, C의 '어느 시간대든'은 지문의 '야간 소멸'과 바로 충돌한다. D는 지문에 근거가 전혀 없는 인과 역전이다. A만 '한계'와 '좁은 역할'을 모두 담고 있어 표면 대조만으로 고를 수 있으므로 전형적 medium 수준이다. 공간 한계만 빠뜨린 부분 반영 선택지처럼, 정답과 미세하게 다른 함정이 없다.

problem.passage:
For decades, ecologists assumed that the bright yellow lichens coating seaside rocks in northern Norway were a single species whose color came from a pigment that shields it from intense summer sunlight. A 2021 survey complicated that picture: lichens growing on shaded north-facing cliffs, where sunlight is weak, were just as yellow as those on exposed south-facing ledges. __Genetic sequencing then revealed that the shaded and exposed populations were not one species but two, distinguishable only at the molecular level.__ Because the two species may have evolved their yellow coloring for unrelated reasons, the shaded-cliff results no longer count as evidence against the sun-shield hypothesis for the exposed population, and researchers are now testing that hypothesis on each species separately.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: For decades, ecologists assumed that the bright yellow lichens coating seaside rocks in northern Norway were a single species whose color came from a pigment that shields it from intense summer sunlight. A 2021 survey complicated that picture: lichens growing on shaded north-facing cliffs, where sunlight is weak, were just as yellow as those on exposed south-facing ledges. __Genetic sequencing then revealed that the shaded and exposed populations were not one species but two, distinguishable only at the molecular level.__ Because the two species may have evolved their yellow coloring for unrelated reasons, the shaded-cliff results no longer count as evidence against the sun-shield hypothesis for the exposed population, and researchers are now testing that hypothesis on each species separately.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that undercuts the assumption behind the survey's apparent challenge, setting up the conclusion that the original hypothesis can still be tested.
It supplies further evidence that the pigment in the lichens does not serve to protect them from sunlight.
It describes the survey result that first cast doubt on the idea that the lichens' color is a sun shield.
It states the text's main purpose, which is to show that molecular methods have replaced field surveys in ecology.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 조사 결과(그늘에서도 노랗다)는 '단일 종'이라는 전제에서만 햇빛 차단 가설을 반박한다. 밑줄 문장은 그 전제를 무너뜨려(두 종), 마지막 문장의 결론(가설은 반박되지 않았고 종별로 검증)을 예비한다. 두 단계(전제 약화→결론 연결)를 모두 봐야 한다.
B(한 단계만 본 역할): 밑줄 문장을 앞선 반박의 연장으로만 읽은 것. 실제로는 반박을 약화시킨다.
C(인접 문장과 혼동): 의문을 제기한 것은 바로 앞 문장(2021 조사)의 기능이다.
D(전체 목적과 개별 기능 뒤바꿈): 분자 방법이 현장조사를 대체했다는 것은 지문 전체 목적도 아니며, 한 문장의 기능을 전체 주제로 격상시킨 오류다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, A: The survey only seemed to challenge the sun-shield hypothesis because everyone assumed the lichens were a single species. The underlined sentence knocks out that assumption by showing there are two species. That sets up the final sentence's conclusion: the hypothesis hasn't been refuted, and it can now be tested on each species separately. To get A, you have to connect both steps: the sentence weakens the assumption, and that leads to the conclusion.
B is wrong because it looks at only one step. It reads the sentence as more evidence against the hypothesis, but the sentence actually weakens the case against it.
C is wrong because it mixes up the underlined sentence with the one before it. The previous sentence, about the 2021 survey, is the one that raised doubt.
D is wrong because it swaps one sentence's job for the purpose of the whole text. The text never says molecular methods have replaced field surveys, and that isn't its main purpose.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 가정(단일 종·햇빛 차단)→2021 조사의 외견상 반박→유전자 분석(두 종)→결론(반박 무효, 종별 검증)의 4단계 사슬을 가짐. 밑줄 문장은 조사의 반박이 의존하던 '단일 종' 전제를 무너뜨려 마지막 문장을 예비하므로 A가 정확히 옳음. B는 관계 방향을 뒤집은 오답(반박 강화 vs 약화), C는 직전 문장의 기능, D는 개별 기능을 전체 목적으로 격상한 오답으로 레시피 요건에 부합. 해설은 정답 및 오답 근거를 논리적으로 일관되게 설명하며 오류 없음. 가상 시나리오로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음. 문항 형식은 디지털 SAT 표준에 부합.

advisory.note: 밑줄 문장은 조사 결과가 반증으로 성립하려면 필요했던 '단일 종' 전제를 무너뜨리고, 이어지는 결론으로 연결된다. 그래서 정답 A가 유일하게 옳다. B는 문장의 역할을 반대로 읽었고, C는 바로 앞 문장의 역할과 혼동했으며, D는 지문 전체 목적을 왜곡했다. A의 '여전히 검증할 수 있다'는 표현은 마지막 문장의 '종별로 검증 중이다'와 일치한다. 다만 D는 너무 쉽게 배제되는 약한 오답이다.

problem.passage:
Biologist Karl Weiss has argued that the angular scatter in honeybee waggle dances—successive runs of a single dance can point in directions differing by many degrees—reflects a limit of bee physiology: an error that colonies simply tolerate because it cannot be eliminated. Entomologist Rina Okafor, recording dances in field colonies, found that the scatter is not constant. It is widest when bees advertise food close to the hive and narrows steadily as the advertised source grows more distant. __Nearby forage, she observes, usually consists of broad patches of flowering plants, whereas the distant sources bees advertise are more often single, compact trees in bloom.__ Okafor has not responded to Weiss directly, but her findings bear on his account.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Biologist Karl Weiss has argued that the angular scatter in honeybee waggle dances—successive runs of a single dance can point in directions differing by many degrees—reflects a limit of bee physiology: an error that colonies simply tolerate because it cannot be eliminated. Entomologist Rina Okafor, recording dances in field colonies, found that the scatter is not constant. It is widest when bees advertise food close to the hive and narrows steadily as the advertised source grows more distant. __Nearby forage, she observes, usually consists of broad patches of flowering plants, whereas the distant sources bees advertise are more often single, compact trees in bloom.__ Okafor has not responded to Weiss directly, but her findings bear on his account.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It supplies a detail suggesting that Okafor would likely challenge Weiss's view that dance scatter is merely a tolerated error, since the scatter appears to match the spread of the food source being advertised.
It supplies a detail suggesting that Okafor would likely support Weiss's view that dance scatter is a physiological limit, since bees appear unable to aim precisely when a food source is broad.
It restates the evidence Weiss used to conclude that dance scatter is an unavoidable error, clarifying why he regarded imprecision as a constraint.
It suggests that Okafor would likely argue that Weiss's measurements of dance angles were distorted by the observation methods he used.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Weiss는 산포가 어쩔 수 없이 감수하는 생리적 '오류'라고 본다. Okafor는 산포가 가까운 먹이원일수록 크다는 것을 발견했고, 밑줄 문장은 가까운 먹이원이 넓은 꽃밭이고 먼 먹이원은 좁은 나무라는 점을 덧붙인다. 그러면 산포 정도가 목표물의 넓이에 맞춰져 있는 셈이 되어 단순한 오류라고 보기 어렵다. 따라서 Okafor는 Weiss의 주장에 반박할 것으로 추론된다. 지문은 이 반응을 직접 말하지 않는다.
B(입장 뒤바꿈): 같은 내용을 근거로 Okafor가 Weiss에게 동의한다고 정반대로 서술했다. 산포가 목표물의 넓이에 맞게 달라진다는 것은 고정된 생리적 한계와 어긋난다.
C(한쪽 입장만 사용): 밑줄 문장은 Okafor의 관찰이지 Weiss가 내세운 근거가 아니다. Weiss의 입장만 보고 기능을 해석한 것이다.
D(지어낸 반응): 측정 방법의 왜곡은 지문 어디에도 나오지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, A: Weiss says the scatter is a physiological error that bees can't avoid and that colonies just put up with. Okafor found that the scatter is largest for food close to the hive. The underlined sentence adds that nearby food tends to be a broad patch, while distant food is usually one compact tree. Put those together and the scatter seems to match how spread out the target is, so it doesn't look like simple error. That suggests Okafor would challenge Weiss, even though the text never says so directly.
B swaps the stances. It uses the same detail to claim Okafor would agree with Weiss. But scatter that changes with the size of the target doesn't fit the idea of a fixed physical limit.
C looks only at one side. The underlined sentence reports Okafor's observation, not evidence Weiss used.
D makes up a reaction. The text never mentions problems with how Weiss measured the dances.

hardJudge.note: Weiss(생리적 한계·감수되는 오류)와 Okafor(거리별 산포 변화 관찰)의 입장이 명확히 구분되고, 지문은 "Okafor has not responded directly"라고 명시해 반응을 추론하도록 요구함. 밑줄 문장은 산포 패턴(가까움=넓음, 멂=좁음)과 먹이원 형태(넓은 꽃밭 vs 단일 나무)를 연결하는 두 번째 단계의 근거로, 이를 종합해야 "산포가 목표물 크기에 맞춰 조정된다 → 단순 오류가 아님"이라는 결론에 도달하므로 A가 유일하게 타당. B는 동일 근거를 반대 결론으로 연결한 입장 뒤바꿈, C는 Weiss의 근거로 오인한 한쪽 입장 오답, D는 지문에 없는 측정 방법 왜곡을 지어낸 오답. 해설과 정답 일치, 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음. 실제 꿀벌 연구(Tautz/Weihmann 등의 tuned-error 가설)와 유사한 소재이나 인물명과 서술은 가공이며 특정 저작물 복제로 보이지 않음.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 맞다. 이를 고르려면 세 가지를 연결해야 한다. 산포는 먹이원이 가까울수록 크고, 가까운 먹이원은 넓은 꽃밭이며, 그렇다면 산포는 목표물의 크기에 맞춘 적응으로 볼 수 있다. 여기서 Weiss의 '감수하는 오류'설을 Okafor가 반박할 것이라는 점을 간접적으로 추론해야 한다. B는 입장을 뒤집은 오답, C는 한쪽 입장만 근거로 삼은 오답, D는 지문에 없는 내용을 지어낸 오답이다.

problem.passage:
Urban planners have long assumed that adding protected bike lanes reduces car traffic on the streets where they are built. To test this, transportation researcher Imani Okafor compared twelve commercial corridors in Rotterdam that received protected lanes with twelve similar corridors that did not. Two years later, bicycle trips on the upgraded corridors had risen by 38 percent, while car volumes on those same corridors were statistically unchanged. __Okafor notes, however, that delivery-vehicle stops on the upgraded corridors fell by nearly a quarter, largely because several shops shifted to cargo-bike couriers once the lanes made such deliveries practical.__ She concludes that protected lanes may not thin general car traffic, but they can reshape one particular category of motor-vehicle use where an alternative becomes viable.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Urban planners have long assumed that adding protected bike lanes reduces car traffic on the streets where they are built. To test this, transportation researcher Imani Okafor compared twelve commercial corridors in Rotterdam that received protected lanes with twelve similar corridors that did not. Two years later, bicycle trips on the upgraded corridors had risen by 38 percent, while car volumes on those same corridors were statistically unchanged. __Okafor notes, however, that delivery-vehicle stops on the upgraded corridors fell by nearly a quarter, largely because several shops shifted to cargo-bike couriers once the lanes made such deliveries practical.__ She concludes that protected lanes may not thin general car traffic, but they can reshape one particular category of motor-vehicle use where an alternative becomes viable.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that supports a narrower claim about motor-vehicle use than the one planners had assumed, a claim that holds where a practical alternative exists.
It offers evidence that, contrary to the overall car-volume results, protected bike lanes reduce motor-vehicle traffic on the corridors where they are installed.
It notes a minor exception to the study's results concerning delivery vehicles that does not bear on the conclusion Okafor ultimately draws.
It suggests that shops' adoption of cargo-bike couriers was what prompted the city to install protected lanes on the upgraded corridors.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 배송 차량 정차가 줄었다는 결과를 제시하며, 이는 '일반 차량 교통 감소'라는 넓은 가정이 아니라 '대안이 실현 가능할 때 특정 범주의 차량 사용이 바뀐다'는 좁고 조건부인 결론을 정확히 뒷받침한다. 근거의 범위와 결론의 범위가 일치한다.
B(과장): 배송 차량이라는 한 범주의 감소를 차량 교통 전반의 감소로 확대 해석했다. 지문은 전체 차량 통행량이 변하지 않았다고 밝힌다.
C(부분 반영·축소): 이 결과를 결론과 무관한 사소한 예외로 보지만, 실제로 Okafor의 최종 결론은 바로 이 결과에 근거한다.
D(인과 역전): 지문에서는 자전거 도로 덕분에 상점들이 카고바이크로 전환했는데, D는 상점들의 전환이 도로 설치를 이끌었다고 인과를 뒤집었다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The underlined sentence reports that delivery-vehicle stops dropped. This finding doesn't support the planners' broad assumption that general car traffic goes down. Instead, it supports Okafor's narrower, conditional conclusion: protected lanes can change one category of motor-vehicle use when a practical alternative becomes available. The scope of the evidence matches the scope of the claim exactly.
B overstates the evidence. It takes a drop in one category, delivery vehicles, and treats it as a drop in motor-vehicle traffic overall. But the text says overall car volumes stayed the same.
C reads the evidence too narrowly. It calls the finding a minor exception that has nothing to do with the conclusion, but Okafor's final conclusion is built directly on this finding.
D reverses cause and effect. In the text, the lanes made cargo-bike deliveries practical, which led shops to switch. D says the shops' switch is what led the city to build the lanes.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 '전체 차량 통행량 불변'이라는 선행 결과와 대비(however)되며, '대안이 실현 가능한 특정 범주'라는 조건부·좁은 결론의 직접 근거로 기능한다. A는 가정(넓음)-결과(불변)-추가 발견(특정 범주)-결론(조건부)의 4단계 사슬을 정확히 반영. B는 범주→전반 과장, C는 결론과의 연결 부정(축소), D는 '도로→카고바이크 전환'을 뒤집은 인과 역전으로 각 오답 유형이 명확히 분리됨. 정답 도출에 가정·null 결과·conclusion 세 요소를 동시에 추적해야 하므로 medium을 넘어서는 통합 사고를 요구. 지문·선택지 형식 및 해설 모두 일관.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 옳다. 근거 범위(배송 차량, 대안이 실현 가능한 경우)와 결론 범위가 일치한다. B는 과장, D는 인과 역전 오답이다. C는 근거를 결론과 무관하다고 보는 오답이라 '근거의 일부만 반영한 좁은 해석' 항목을 엄밀히 충족하지 못한다. A만 'narrower'와 조건부 표현을 써서 다소 눈에 띄지만, hard 수준으로는 수용 가능하다.

problem.passage:
Botanist Hope Reyes studied two shrubs on a dry hillside. Sagebrush sheds most of its leaves each summer, a habit that limits water loss. Saltbush, rooted right beside the sagebrush, keeps its leaves through the hottest months. ______ it loses surprisingly little water: a crust of salt crystals on its leaves reflects much of the sunlight.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Botanist Hope Reyes studied two shrubs on a dry hillside. Sagebrush sheds most of its leaves each summer, a habit that limits water loss. Saltbush, rooted right beside the sagebrush, keeps its leaves through the hottest months. ______ it loses surprisingly little water: a crust of salt crystals on its leaves reflects much of the sunlight.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
Likewise,
As a result,
In other words,
problem.explanation:
정답 A. 'it'는 바로 앞의 sagebrush가 아니라 앞 문장의 주어 Saltbush를 가리킨다. 한여름에도 잎을 유지하면 보통 수분을 많이 잃을 것이라 예상되는데, 실제로는 손실이 적으므로 예상과 반대되는 결과를 잇는 'Nevertheless,'가 알맞다.
B(Likewise): 'it'를 인접 명사 sagebrush로 보거나, sagebrush가 물을 아끼는 것과 같은 방식이라고 본 오답이다. 하지만 saltbush는 잎을 떨어뜨리지 않으므로 같은 방식이 아니며, 바로 앞 문장(잎 유지)과는 대비 관계다.
C(As a result): 문법상 자연스럽지만 잎을 유지하는 것이 수분 손실 감소의 원인이 되지는 않는다. 실제 원인은 콜론 뒤에 나오는 소금 결정이다.
D(In other words): '수분 손실이 적다'를 '잎을 유지한다'의 재진술로 보는데, 서로 다른 내용이므로 재진술이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
Answer: A. The pronoun "it" refers to Saltbush, the subject of the previous sentence, not to "sagebrush," the noun right next to it. Saltbush keeps its leaves through the hottest months, so you would expect it to lose a lot of water. Instead, it loses little. "Nevertheless" correctly signals this unexpected result.
B is wrong because "Likewise" treats saltbush as using the same strategy as sagebrush (or wrongly takes "it" to mean sagebrush). Saltbush does not shed its leaves, and the sentence right before the blank sets up a contrast, not a similarity.
C is wrong because keeping leaves does not cause low water loss. The cause is the salt crust described after the colon.
D is wrong because losing little water is not a restatement of keeping leaves. These are two different ideas.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 타당: 'it'=Saltbush이며, 잎 유지→수분 손실 많을 것이라는 암묵적 기대(첫 문장의 sagebrush 원리에서 도출)와 실제 결과의 대비. 다만 'surprisingly'가 강한 단서로 작용해 추론 부담이 다소 줄어드는 점은 약점. 삽입구 'rooted right beside the sagebrush'로 인접 명사 오인 유도 설계는 충족. 사실관계(sagebrush 여름 낙엽, saltbush 소금 결정 반사) 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 'it'는 바로 앞 문장의 주어 Saltbush를 가리키는데, 이는 매우 자연스러운 지시라서 비국소적 지시 추적이라는 설계 의도가 거의 구현되지 않았다. 문항은 결국 '잎 유지 → 예상 밖의 적은 수분 손실'을 잇는 전형적인 양보 전환어 문항으로, medium 수준이다. 'Likewise'는 sagebrush와 결과가 비슷하다는 점에서 어느 정도 그럴듯하지만, 'surprisingly'가 대비를 분명히 하므로 정답 A는 유일하게 성립한다.

problem.passage:
Ecologist Hans Slabbekoorn and colleagues observed that great tits living near busy roads sing at noticeably higher pitches than great tits in forests, a pattern widely attributed to birds raising their pitch so their songs are not masked by low-frequency traffic noise. Yet when researchers recorded the same urban birds in the early morning hours, when the roads were nearly silent, the birds still sang at the elevated pitches. ______ the higher pitch seems to be a lasting feature of urban great tits' songs, likely shaped by noise over time, rather than a moment-to-moment adjustment to whatever noise is present.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Ecologist Hans Slabbekoorn and colleagues observed that great tits living near busy roads sing at noticeably higher pitches than great tits in forests, a pattern widely attributed to birds raising their pitch so their songs are not masked by low-frequency traffic noise. Yet when researchers recorded the same urban birds in the early morning hours, when the roads were nearly silent, the birds still sang at the elevated pitches. ______ the higher pitch seems to be a lasting feature of urban great tits' songs, likely shaped by noise over time, rather than a moment-to-moment adjustment to whatever noise is present.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: However,
For example,
Similarly,
Taken together,
problem.explanation:
정답 D. 첫 관찰(도로 근처 새의 음높이가 높고 소음 탓으로 여겨짐)과 둘째 관찰(조용한 시간에도 높은 음높이 유지)은 언뜻 충돌한다. 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 합쳐 '소음이 오랜 시간에 걸쳐 만든 지속적 특성이지 즉각적 조정이 아니다'라고 결론 내린다. 소음의 역할(관찰 1)과 지속성(관찰 2)을 모두 담으므로 종합을 나타내는 'Taken together,'가 맞다.
A(However): 두 관찰이 상반돼 보인다는 점만 보고 대조로 처리한 오답이다. 마지막 문장은 바로 앞 문장을 반박하지 않고 오히려 그 문장에서 결론을 끌어낸다.
B(For example): 둘째 관찰 하나만 반영한 오답이다. 마지막 문장은 앞 내용의 구체적 사례가 아니라 앞 내용에서 끌어낸 일반적 결론이다.
C(Similarly): 앞 문장과 비슷한 다른 사실을 하나 더 덧붙인다는 뜻이라 종합 결론과 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is D. The first observation (birds near roads sing at higher pitches, which is credited to traffic noise) and the second (the birds keep singing high even when the roads are quiet) seem to clash. The last sentence combines them: noise probably shaped the pitch over time (from observation 1), but the high pitch is a lasting trait, not an on-the-spot adjustment (from observation 2). Since it draws on both, "Taken together," fits.
A (However) treats the two observations as a simple contrast. But the final sentence doesn't push back against the sentence before it. It draws a conclusion from that sentence.
B (For example) relies on the second observation alone. The final sentence isn't a specific example of what came before. It's a general conclusion drawn from it.
C (Similarly) would add another fact like the one before it. That doesn't match a conclusion that combines both findings.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 타당: 마지막 문장은 직전 문장을 반박하지 않고(A 배제) 두 관찰을 통합해 결론을 내리므로 'Taken together,'가 적절. A는 'Yet'으로 이미 처리된 대조를 반복 적용하는 함정으로 잘 작동함. 다만 체크리스트 3('한쪽 관찰만 반영한 전환어')에 해당하는 오답이 실질적으로 없음—B는 예시 오류, C는 유사 추가 오류로 모두 '한쪽 관찰 반영'과는 거리가 있음. 'Therefore' 류가 정답과 경합할 수 있어 배제한 것으로 보이나 그 결과 레시피 항목 3이 비어 있음. Slabbekoorn의 도시 박새 음높이 연구는 실존하며 지문 서술은 원문 복제 아님.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 타당하다. 다만 'Yet'으로 이미 대조가 드러나 있어서 However가 꽤 매력적인 오답이 되고, 이것이 난이도를 만든다. 한쪽 관찰만 반영한 오답 설계는 약하다. B는 실제로는 관계 유형이 틀린 오답이다. 'Thus/Therefore' 같은 다른 결론 전환어가 선택지에 없으므로 정답은 유일하다.

problem.passage:
Biologist Rana Okafor studied two groups of salamanders living in the same Ozark cave. Salamanders in the upper chambers, which receive faint light from the entrance, keep small but working eyes. ______ salamanders in the deepest chambers, like the blind cavefish that share their pools, have lost functional eyes entirely.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Biologist Rana Okafor studied two groups of salamanders living in the same Ozark cave. Salamanders in the upper chambers, which receive faint light from the entrance, keep small but working eyes. ______ salamanders in the deepest chambers, like the blind cavefish that share their pools, have lost functional eyes entirely.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
As a result,
By contrast,
For example,
problem.explanation:
정답 C. 마지막 문장의 주어는 '가장 깊은 방의 도롱뇽'이고, 이는 앞 문장의 '위쪽 방의 도롱뇽'(작지만 기능하는 눈을 유지)과 비교된다. 눈이 있는 쪽과 눈을 완전히 잃은 쪽이 대비되므로 'By contrast,'가 맞다. 'like the blind cavefish'라는 비교 표현은 주어가 동굴어와 비슷하다는 뜻일 뿐이며, 전환어가 연결해야 하는 앞 문장의 대상과는 관계가 없다.
A(Similarly): 바로 옆의 '눈먼 동굴어'를 기준으로 삼아 유사성을 읽은 오답이다. 전환어는 앞 문장과의 관계를 나타내야 하는데, 앞 문장은 눈이 있는 도롱뇽을 다룬다.
B(As a result): 문법적으로는 자연스럽다. 그러나 위쪽 도롱뇽이 눈을 유지한다는 사실이 깊은 곳 도롱뇽이 눈을 잃은 원인이 될 수는 없다.
D(For example): 지문 전체 주제인 '두 집단'을 지시 대상으로 삼아 마지막 문장을 그 사례로 본 오답이다. 실제로는 두 번째 집단을 첫 번째 집단과 대비하는 문장이지 앞 문장의 예시가 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
C is correct. The subject of the last sentence is the salamanders in the deepest chambers. They are compared with the salamanders in the upper chambers from the previous sentence, which keep working eyes. One group has eyes and the other has lost them entirely, so "By contrast," fits. The phrase "like the blind cavefish" only says that the deep salamanders resemble the cavefish. It doesn't describe how this sentence relates to the previous one.
A ("Similarly,") is wrong because it treats the nearby noun "cavefish" as the point of comparison. The transition has to link back to the previous sentence, and that sentence describes salamanders that still have eyes.
B ("As a result,") sounds grammatical, but it doesn't make sense. The upper salamanders keeping their eyes can't cause the deep salamanders to lose theirs.
D ("For example,") treats the last sentence as an example of the "two groups" mentioned at the start. In fact, the sentence sets the second group against the first. It isn't an example of the previous sentence.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(눈을 유지한 위쪽 도롱뇽)과 마지막 문장(눈을 잃은 깊은 곳 도롱뇽)의 대비이므로 'By contrast'가 유일하게 타당. 삽입구 'like the blind cavefish'가 인접 유사성 신호로 작용해 A(Similarly)를 유인하며, B는 문법적으로만 자연스러운 인과 오답, D는 주제 전체를 지시 대상으로 오인한 오답으로 레시피 요건을 충족. 문장은 짧고 단순하며 사실 관계(오자크 동굴 도롱뇽·눈먼 동굴어)도 무리 없음. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 모순 없이 뒷받침함. 가상의 인물 사용으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 삽입된 비교구 'like the blind cavefish'가 Similarly 쪽으로 유도하는 함정이다. 전환어는 이 비교구가 아니라 앞 문장의 위쪽 도롱뇽과의 관계를 기준으로 골라야 한다. 다만 눈을 유지한 집단과 눈을 잃은 집단의 대비가 꽤 분명해서 hard 수준으로는 경계선에 가깝다.

problem.passage:
Between 2009 and 2016, linguist Mara Okonjo documented Tuwali, a language spoken by fewer than 3,000 people, while working with a small grant that covered only two field seasons. Okonjo has stressed that her goal was never to produce an exhaustive dictionary of the language; rather, she wanted to record how speakers actually use Tuwali when joking, bargaining, and telling stories to one another. ______ her archive contains relatively few formal word lists but more than 400 hours of unscripted conversation.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Between 2009 and 2016, linguist Mara Okonjo documented Tuwali, a language spoken by fewer than 3,000 people, while working with a small grant that covered only two field seasons. Okonjo has stressed that her goal was never to produce an exhaustive dictionary of the language; rather, she wanted to record how speakers actually use Tuwali when joking, bargaining, and telling stories to one another. ______ her archive contains relatively few formal word lists but more than 400 hours of unscripted conversation.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
Accordingly,
Similarly,
Earlier,
problem.explanation:
